                                                           Welcome to our church in Lee, MA!

What makes Berkshire Hills Baptist Church so special? Very simply, it is the people. BHBC is a church filled with caring, loving, and friendly people.

Our church is here to serve you through regular weekly ministries as well as special activities throughout the year. It is here that relationships are made and where Christ is magnified. title: Family Series
html:
May & June 2012 - Series on the Family

Feel free to download and listen to these online sermons preached at the Pulpit of Berkshire Hills Baptist Church.  We preach the truth in love and we pray that the Holy Spirit will bring a great blessing upon the preaching of His Holy Word.  Blessings.  Web Site Administrator. 

06.17.2012 - Fathers of the Family - Matthew 7:6-12 - Pastor Doug Mann

Dads, the lion of the family.
What kind of father would give his children the wrong things or gifts they did not need? If God, our heavenly Father, gives to us what we need - how much more we who are earthly parents? How does the Golden rule equate to fathership? Find out in this much needed sermon for our time. 


Use the player below to listen or:  Download sermon by right clicking here.

June 10, 2012:  Children are a Heritage of the Lord - Psalms 127 -
Pastor Doug Mann.  

Psalm 127 - What does it mean that children are a heritage of the Lord? This message is for all those with children or grandchildren who want to know if it really is important to raise our children in the ways of God. What will happen if we don't raise our children in God's way?


Use the player below to listen or:  Download sermon by right clicking here.

June 3, 2012: Family Growth Part 2 - Philippians 1:20-21

Listen to this sermon to learn what God has for you, no matter what lot you are in life: young adult, middle age, or seasoned saints will all receive important information on the struggles we face in life, the strategies to learn to be Christ like, and the preparation to face death with joy! 


Use the player below to listen or:  Download sermon by right clicking here.

May 27, 2012: Family Growth Part 1 - 2 Peter 3:18 

In this sermon, Pastor Doug Mann teaches how to "grow in grace and in the knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ." Learn specifically about raising children and teaching them the right way to go. You will also learn how you must vigilant to see all the "water moccasins" your children may not see in their lives. 

Use the player below to listen or:  Download sermon by right clicking here.

May 20, 2012:  Family Series:  Marriage - Proverbs 18:22 - Peter James

Marriage is a gift from the LORD; explore the Word of God to find out why it is that God finds marriage so precious.  Also hear what it is the LORD expects of the man in marriage; what does it mean to love the wife, to honor her, and to love her?

And finally, learn the purpose of marriage:  to show forth God's glory to the end of the world!  

Use the player below to listen or:  Download sermon by right clicking here.

May 13, 2012:  Mothers - Ephesians 6:1-4 - Pastor Doug Mann

While we know the Bible teaches that children should obey their parents, did you know this is the LORD's will? We often assume the first 4 commandments are related to our relationship to God; but what if the fifth commandment is also related to our relationship with God. Is it possible that God expects us to respect our mothers, else we are out of His will? 


Use the player below to listen or:  Download sermon by right clicking here.

May 6, 2012:  A Functioning Family - Joshua 24:14-15: [Sermon #1 in Series] - Pastor Doug Mann

In order for our families to function properly, God must be the center of our family life. But exactly who is God, what is He like, and why should we serve Him? Find out in our first sermon in a series - A Functioning Family from Joshua 24:14-15.  


Use the player below to listen or: Download sermon by right clicking here.

Vacation Bible School 2016

Welcome to Ocean Commotion!

Welcome to Ocean Commotion, where your divers will dive deep into God’s Word to learn about Noah and the Flood of his day (Genesis 6–8)!

Every day, our kids are challenged to stand for God in their schools, among their friends, in our culture . . . no matter what. And they’re bombarded with the lie that God’s Word isn’t true when it talks about earthly things (rocks, fossils), so it can’t be trusted to tell the truth about spiritual things.

Noah experienced the same challenges during the time of the great Flood thousands of years ago. Yet, by God’s grace, he was able to Stand for God, Obey God, Trust God, Thank God, and Fear God . . . no matter what. The biggest watery catastrophe the world has ever known happened during his lifetime. But through it all, Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord.

At this Vacation Bible School program, your kids will dive deep into the account of Noah and the Flood from the book of Genesis! They’ll learn to apply the spiritual lessons from Noah’s life to their own. And, along the way, they’ll uncover earthly lessons from the Flood: how all the animals fit on the Ark, how the Flood covered the whole Earth, and how we can still see the effects of this Flood today. They’ll also learn that the flood legends from around the world are based on the true account in Genesis!

Prepare for a boatload of excitement at Ocean Commotion, VBS for 2016!

Coronavirus Update, 03/14/2020

In light of the statement below, we will be cancelling our Wednesday Evening prayer service until further notice.

With so much in the news about the coronavirus (COVID-19), it's hard to separate facts from hyperbole. We want to protect the flock, while ensuring we do not cause any undue panic.

As such, we believe it's appropriate for our church to take precautionary measures to ensure that we do everything possible to keep COVID-19 at bay. This is especially important as we have people of all ages who may be particularly susceptible to the virus.

As a church, we are taking the following precautions, and we ask that you help us keep these protocols in place for the next several weeks:

     • Avoid personal contact such as handshaking. We will suspend our typical handshaking time on Sunday morning.

     • Use hand sanitizer or wash your hands for 20 seconds when arriving at church.

     • If you feel ill and have any of the possible symptoms of COVID-19 (runny nose, sore throat, persistent cough, fever), please do not attend church until symptoms subside.

     • If you have been in contact with anyone who has tested positive for COVID-19, or if you have been in contact with anyone who recently traveled abroad, please self-quarantine for 14 days before returning to church.

Thank you for helping us put these precautions in place!

title: Doctrine
html:
Doctrinal Statement

Berkshire Hills Baptist Church

STATEMENT OF DOCTRINE

as of October 24, 2010



1. The Holy Scriptures: We believe the Old and New Testaments of the Holy Bible in its original writings is the verbally and plenary inspired word and revelation of God; that it is literally true from Genesis 1:1 to Revelation 22:21; and, therefore, we look to it as our only authority in matters of faith, practice, and daily living. The King James Version of the Bible shall be the official and only translation used for preaching and teaching by the church. II Tim. 3:16,17; II Peter 1:19-21.

2. The Godhead: We believe that God is the only eternal and uncreated Being, is infinite and perfect in all His attributes, and has revealed Himself as the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, who are coequal and coordinate in their distinct but harmonious offices. Isa. 44:6; Psa. 90:2; 145:3 Matt. 5:48 Deut. 32:4;

Matt. 28:19; Jn. 14:16,17; 10:30.

3. The Person and Work of Christ: We believe in the absolute deity of the Son, the Lord Jesus Christ1; that He is the Creator and Sustainer of all things2; that He was conceived by the Holy Spirit and born of the Virgin Mary3; that He lived sinless among men4 that He died on the cross as a substitute for us shedding His blood for the remission of our sins5: that He was buried6; that He arose physically from the grave7: that He ascended into heaven and in His bodily presence sits at the right hand of the Father ever making intercession for us8; and that He is coming again, visibly and at any moment9. 1Jn.1:1,l4,15,18,29,30; Lk. 3:22. 2Jn. 1:3: Col. 1:6,17; 3Lk. 1:31,35; Isa. 7:14; Matt.1:18-25. 4Jn. 8:46 Heb. 4:14,15; 7:26-28.5Matt. 26:28; I Cor. 15:3; I Pet. 2:24; Heb. 9:22b; Eph. 2:13. 6Jn. 12:24; I Cor 15:4a; 7Psa. 16:10; Jn. 2:19, 21, 22; Mat. 28:6a; I Cor. 15:4b. 8Acts 1:9; 7:55, 56; Col. 3:11; Heb. 7:25; I Jn. 2:1. 9Acts 1:11; I Thes. 4:16; Zech. 14:4.

4. title: Forgot God’s will?  Time to take a u-turn.
html:
"13 Go to now, ye that say, To day or to morrow we will go into such a city, and continue there a year, and buy and sell, and get gain:  14 Whereas ye know not what shall be on the morrow. For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away.  15 For that ye ought to say, If the Lord will, we shall live, and do this, or that."

James 4:13-15
The most often asked question from Christians is this:  how can I know what God wants me to do in my life?  Have you been disappointed not receiving the answer, or receiving an answer you didn’t think was the right one?

If you are asking about God’s will, you are already on the right track!   Don’t be like the merchants of James 4:13 who decided to ignore God’s plan all together and make their own plan.  They decided to buy goods at one town and resell the same goods in another town to gain a large profit; they felt they could make a lot of money.  They never thought to themselves, will the Lord give us another day to do this?
If you are asking about God’s will, you will find that God will lead you on a journey you never thought you would take.  God has a personalized plan for you; don’t abandon Him to follow your own plan.  Future Pastors, missionaries, worship leaders, or Sunday School teachers have forsaken God’s will for prizes or prestige; when they stand before the judgment seat of Christ, they will be filled with many regrets on what they could have done for Him.  

If you are asking about God’s will because you don’t want to do what He has already asked you to do, remember that His will are not requests.  They are His marching orders; as a good soldier of Christ, participate fully in the will of the Lord in your life and take the path He has laid out for you.  He is not going to mail you a list of suggestions; instead, as you participate in your local church, stay faithful to reading the Bible, and live a life that is holy and pure before Him – He will slowly show you the place He has for you in His kingdom.   

Think about this:  

How much farther along would God’s church be if everyone did what He asked them to do?  What are the missed opportunities you never knew about because you decided it would be your way, not His?  Good news. You can begin the grand adventure now; turn off the wrong path, take a major U-turn, and follow after Him!

Listen to the entire sermon below:

10.13.2013 - Where There's a Will, There's Some Sway

title: 1 Corinthians 10:13 - A Way of Escape for those who suffer
html:
“There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.”  1 Corinthians 10:13
Have you ever felt like the prophet Elijah who believed everyone was against him and that no one was suffering for God like he was? (1 Kings 18:22)  It is tempting to feel, in the midst of terrible suffering and persecution, that we are the only ones that know and understand what we are going through.  But today’s scriptures says there is no “temptation” (or testing, or trial) that is not common to man; while we may honestly believe we are alone in our woes – a quick survey of support groups in our local area might show that others deal with the common struggles of life.  (As an aside, these support groups need many more Christians to gently share a Christ centered way of recovery.)

Even in the feelings of loneliness, know this:  God is faithful.  He will do two things for us in the midst of seeming unbearable suffering:  a) He will not allow us to bear more than we can handle and b) He will make a way of escape in the suffering.  While this is comforting when we are not suffering, it can be difficult to believe when we are suffering.  It is at this time you need to exercise faith to know that you are not alone and that the Lord will provide an end to the affliction.  And who knows?  The experiences you go through today may very well make you stronger so you can be an answer to prayers for someone else tomorrow!

title: 1 John 2:15 - Growing in a Holy Lifestyle - Rotten Apples?
html:
Sometimes we vacillate in our Christian walk: one moment we're a holy person; another moment, we're a worldly person. 
If we are children of the most High, He wants us to act like a child of God all the time.


If you are a good apple and you throw yourself on a barrel of rotten apples – you will not automatically make the other apples good. The good apple becomes rotten if it is left in the barrel; however, if it is soon removed, it will not be corrupted. When 1 John 2:15-17 tells us “love not the world” (in other words, we are in the world and not of the world) this means that we are not to fall in love with worldly affections. When dealing with unbelievers, we are not to avoid them. We are allowed to place ourselves with them as Jesus did, give them the gospel of Christ, and then remove ourselves before we begin to adopt their worldly attitudes. Holiness is not just staying away from unholiness; holiness is realizing that you can talk and even befriend the unsaved without falling into their unholy lifestyle.

1 John 2:15 "Love not the world, neither the things that are in the world. If any man love the world, the love of the Father is not in him."

title: 2 Peter 3:12:  Grow in Grace by Looking for His Appearing
html:
Are you ready for Jesus’s “any moment” return when the Trump of God sounds and we are gathered together with all saints; then “so shall we ever be with the Lord” (1 Thessalonians 4:17)?  

Part of growing in grace is being conscious that the Lord will return at any time. 

What would it be like if you weren’t paying attention and you decided to give in to temptation and disobey God?  Right at the moment you sin, the trumpet of the Lord sounds and you are Raptured to be with Him … the first thing you see is the LORD, right as you were sinning!  No wonder some may be “ashamed of Him” at His coming. (1 John 2:28)            

Or another scenario: suppose you are with unbelievers and instead of witnessing Christ’s free gospel of grace to them, you are mocking them, telling them unholy jokes, or joining them in sin?  Then the trumpet sounds and you disappear; what impression will you have left with your unsaved loved ones?  Will that person ever come to Christ? 

So, let’s always think about His return so that everything we do in word or deed might give glory to Our Heavenly Father and purify ourselves even as He is pure!  (1 John 3:3)


Are you excited to live in God's grace?  Then keep reading our blog, or listen to the full sermon below.

title: 1 Peter 5:10 - Can suffering heal us?
html:
"But the God of all grace, who hath called us unto his eternal glory by Christ Jesus, after that ye have suffered a while, make you perfect, stablish, strengthen, settle you." 1 Peter 5:10
No man or woman is born great; we were all, at one time, babies.  So too, if you are longing for strong faith that grabs hold of the hem of Jesus – It will take time.  Suffering is not meant to make us feel like martyrs; nor is it meant to give us something to complain to others about.  Instead, suffering is given to us so we can grow in the faith of Christ.  For a little while, we will suffer.

But suffering is the method  of growth; no one’s faith is worth much if it hasn’t been tried.  And while we would never ask to go through suffering or pray that others would go through terrible turmoil, we know the Lord allows tests to build up our character.  Peter tells us its purpose is to “perfect” us.  


In ancient Israel, fishermen would throw large nets into the sea to catch many fish.  They would pull in their catch, but inevitably the work of the net was sometimes so great – it would get torn holding all the fish or being cast against the rocks.  The fishermen would then “perfect” or “mend” their nets so that they could be useful again.  So too, God is “mending” you through the very thing you are afraid of:  the pain of suffering.  Don’t feel sorry for yourself; don’t believe that somehow, God is mad at you; and don’t turn your back on God because you’d rather experience prosperity.  Instead, pray  - Lord, please teach me Your ways, help me to have a heart like Your heart, and mend me so I can be useful again to You.  Amen.

title: 1 Peter 5:10 - Suffering a Good Thing?
html:
In contemporary Christianity, many have focused on the gifts of God that make us feel good; be they riches, comfort of life, great employment, or good health – who ever heard of suffering being a good thing?  Even more, could suffering actually be a type of grace that God uses in our life? Yes, suffering can both lead and protect us.

For instance, the disciples and Jesus decided to go over to the other side of a lake in a small ship; while Jesus was asleep, the disciples were afraid because of the wind and rains!  (Luke 8:22-25)  Immediately, Jesus calmed the seas after the disciples fearfully awoke Him.  Yet, what if they had not awakened the Master?  Could the sea and the winds actually have moved the boat to where they needed to be instead of the disciples having to row?  Maybe our suffering is meant to lead us to places that others cannot go, such as helping others with cancer, with special needs children, or with  the loss of loved ones?


Corrie Ten Boom (a dutch woman imprisoned in a concentration camp for hiding Jews during World War II) learned to be thankful for lice that were all over her during her internment.  At first, it seemed like cruel suffering … until she learned the guards did not abuse women infested with lice.  It may seem like a small grace in the middle of a greater suffering; but it is actually proof that God works in both the big and small events of life.  Don’t’ fall into the trap of believing God’s riches are only found in material wealth; His riches are imparted many different ways, even in the gift of suffering as difficult as it may be to go through.

title: 1 Peter 5:8 - Grace Overcoming Satan
html:
"Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour"
1 Peter 5:8
While it is true that sometimes circumstances or even self can bring  suffering and pain in our lives, there is also a chance that Satan will be allowed by the Lord to cause us affliction.  In the book of Job, we learn that in order to show a great example of faithfulness in all things, God allowed the devil to cause affliction on Job.

That is why God tells us to be sober and vigilant because our enemy stalks us, ready to “devour” us.  Either the devil, or a lesser evil spirit, can lie to us.  The devil will promise the best, and give us the worst; he’ll promise honor, but give disgrace; he promises profit, but dishes out loss; he promises life, but instead we receive death.  Satan’s promises are no good; he is not like our faithful, all knowing, all existing God!

Both James 4:7 and 1 Peter 5:9 tell us to resist the devil; we need not talk to him, fear him, or try to understand him.  Instead, we simply need to go back to the Lord and ask Him to help us live a holy life.  Furthermore, remember that God is the God of all grace.  Rest in the loving arms of Jesus, and let Him worry about the enemy in your life.  You keep steadfast in the faith, knowing that any wavering or hesitation can be overcome by our good and loving Shepherd.

title: 1 Thessalonnians 5:17:  Take the Phone Book Challenge
html:
In our last blog, we talked about prayer as being a bridge to God’s heart.  As we learn what it means to be personally revived by returning to the Lord, and being restored by His grace – one of the most important things to note is that Christianity is not only about myself, but about others.  For instance, we are to be kind to one another (Ephesians 4:32), forgive one another (Colossians 3:13), and pray for one another (James 5:16)

Years ago, the great evangelist Billy Sunday was preparing for an evangelism campaign in a certain city.  In advance, he called upon the Pastors to provide him with a listing of the names of people who needed the Lord.  The hope was that having the list of names would help Billy pray that their hearts would be prepared to hear the Gospel.  The response?  Billy Sunday was given a phone book for the area.  Apparently, everyone needed prayer!

So here is your challenge for this week:  take one page from the local phone book, and simply pray over all the names you see.  Each person has a different and unique story, struggle, and spiritual battle.  Pray that the Lord will save to the uttermost all these people and that they would grow in the grace and knowledge of Christ.

"Pray without ceasing." 1 Thessalonians 5:17

title: 2 Peter 3:18 -Two Types of Grace
html:
We are to grow in the grace of the Lord Jesus; grace has two different kinds of meaning.  
Grace at first means God’s favor on us when we were undeserving.  When God gave us grace at salvation, we didn’t deserve to be saved or have our sins forgiven.  Yet, because of His grace – he gave to us His unmerited favor which brought about salvation.

After salvation, there is another grace.  This, too, is the grace of Jesus Christ which is, for the Christian, a learning process whereby we become more like Jesus Christ in His image and His likeness.  The type of grace mentioned in 2 Peter 2:18 means to “bestow pleasure” or “delight”.  In other words, as we are learning, growing, and becoming more like Him – we should be delighted to do so!  We should be happy to tell the world that He is the perfect example of how we should live, act, and what we should do.  If I’m a child of God, the only example to look to in our spiritual growth is Jesus.  In other words, He is our life if we are going to grow in the way that God wants us to.

Are you excited to grow in Jesus’s grace?  Continue reading our bi-daily blog which runs Sunday – Friday, or click here and listen to the entire sermon from January 6, 2013.

title: 2 Timothy 1:7 - Grace Exploding with Love!
html:
"For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind." 2 Timothy 2:7
God’s Word tells us that we will suffer for our relationship with Christ; this is true especially when we share His gospel to the world.  Sometimes when we witness for Him, we will look into people’s eyes before opening our mouths and we give up because we think we are going to be rejected anyway.


God did not give us a spirit of fear (cowardice), but rather power (greek: dunamis, from where we get the word dynamite.)  In other words, if we are fearful to be His ambassador to a lost world – that’s on us.  He gave us everything we need:  His Holy Spirit, His power, and His love.

It is a great truth that we have power to bravely go forward as a soldier of the cross and show people the way to eternal life.  However, without love – we would overpower people.  God wants us to be compassionate, so He gave us love.  God does not want us to water down the truth, yet he does not want us to beat people with the truth either.  (You know, you have met some Christians who are very brave but lack tact and compassion when they talk to unbelievers.) 

Our text also tells us that with power and with love, God has also given us a sound mind.  Our thoughts are no longer clouded by darkness or sin, and we are alert to the needs of others around us.  Who else but God, the Creator, knew people would need truth tempered with love so they could come to a relationship with Him?  Maybe I am fearful, unloving, and thinking ungodly thoughts.  No problem:  where sin abounds, grace even more abounds. (Romans 5:20)  Turn back to Him; He will not only take you back, but He will change your heart so you won't want to return to your old ways!

title: 2 Timothy 2:1-3 - Grace Overcoming the "Spin Cycle"
html:
"1 Thou therefore, my son, be strong in the grace that is in Christ Jesus. 2 And the things that thou hast heard of me among many witnesses, the same commit thou to faithful men, who shall be able to teach others also."  2 Timothy 2:1-2
A little boy told the local grocer that his cat ultimately had died; “It must have been that laundry detergent you used to clean him that I told you not to buy” the grocer said.  The boy looked up and quipped, “Nah, the laundry detergent didn’t kill him.  It was the spin cycle!”
Our world can be rough; sometimes we are stuck in the “spin cycle” of life and even after the cycle is over, we can’t seem to recover our balance.  Sadly, some Christians have adopted the idea that they “love Jesus” but they don’t love His church.  Hence, they are floating to and fro every which way, adopting and creating their own form of the spiritual life in Christ, and generally wondering why their walk seems to always flounder.  Unfortunately, they have missed out on the grace that is part of God’s local assembly of believers.  In fact, Paul instructed Timothy (and therefore all Pastors) to be strong in that grace so they can commit the life giving information of the gospel of Jesus to “others also”.

We’re in a spiritual battle; we don’t go to church so we can feel good.  We go to church to encourage one another, to pass on important information about God, and to lift up those who have fallen.  Ultimately, we are here to worship God together.  While worshiping God individually has its place, it is much better to worship Him with fellow Christians.  No more pity parties!  If you've put off being with other Christians, visit a great Bible believing church this week.  Get out of the spin cycle of life; share yourself and your struggles with others.

title: 2 Timothy 2:1 - Grace Strengthening  Soldiers of Christ
html:
"Thou therefore, my son, be strong in the grace that is in Christ Jesus."  2 Timothy 2:1
Soldiers: here are our marching orders as end time saints!  Be strong in the grace that is in Christ Jesus; He is our life and source of strength.  God not only gives strength, but he enables us to perform what He has called us to do.  Paul praised the Lord that he “hath enabled” him, and put him in the ministry (1 Timothy 1:12).  Then he used the same greek work for “enabled” when he asked us to be strong in Christ.
As we walk in life, we will get tired.  We may be tempted to do what the sailors did when they hit the storm in Jonah 2; we might try to get rid of everything we consider baggage.  But some of the “baggage” we might try to get rid of is service to God.  No, let us not abandon our post – but ask the Lord to help us to be faithful in that ministry. 
 
It goes back to our basic view of the Lord and our life.  We might ask our self, “How am I going to fit ministry around my busy schedule?”  Instead, we need to figure out how we are going to fit our busy schedule around the ministry God has called us to.  God doesn’t give us things to do just to keep us busy (although one wonders how many addictions would be squashed if we filled our time serving God.)  He has made us builders of His glorious kingdom that is not shaken; “we shall receive grace by which we shall serve and please God in reverence and in awe.”  (Hebrews 12:28)  So let’s keep building; when we tire, let’s go to God to receive replenishing grace.

Learn more about replenishing grace in the audio sermon below.

title: 2 Timothy 2:2 - Sharing Jesus by Grace
html:
"And the things that thou hast heard of me among many witnesses, the same commit thou to faithful men, who shall be able to teach others also."  2 Timothy 2:2
Part of living as Christians is to teach and show to others what we have been taught by God, specifically the good news that Christ saves to the uttermost those that put their trust in Him.  It may be discouraging because we have told everyone we know; then let's tell others we haven't met.  It may be discouraging because we've run out of people to witness to; then let's tell the same people the same message, but in a different way.  Or maybe we are discouraged because we simply don’t know what to say.  Remember what we were told when we got saved, and let's keep repeating the same message!  You  have to admit, the gospel is always the same:  believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved.  (Romans 10:9-10) 
Speaking of how simple and consistent the gospel message is, don’t be taken in by those who want to “improve” on the gospel with a new, glossy book or strange “new” revelation.  The tried and true message that has been preached from the time of Jesus is the same message we should be telling others today.  While there may be innovative ways in sharing it, the message remains the same.  Hallelujah, we don’t have to make anything up! We just need to trust that the Holy Spirit will take His words and convict men, women, boys, and girls to repent and believe on Him.  Remember, be strong in His grace and He will complete the work in you.

Share your faith now; hit like and share this message with people you know through facebook!

title: A Love that Reaches Out to Those Who Cannot or Will Not Love
html:
"3 We give thanks to God and the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, praying always for you, 4 Since we heard of your faith in Christ Jesus, and of the love which ye have to all the saints" 
Colossians 1:3-4

Can you rejoice at the love that God has placed in your heart for all your neighbors?  Love is not something we can properly do unless God is in our life.

Before we got saved, we loved others the best way we knew how to.  We might have shown others some mercy, we may have done nice things, and we might have really expressed our thankfulness for those we deemed ‘lovable’.  Perhaps we truly tried to help others and, perhaps, we were motivated by some sort of philanthropic, selfless cause.  But unless we showed forth the love of Christ, it was an empty temporal affection that does not really quench our thirst for God.

Once we fall in love with Jesus, He gives us a new commandment:  love another as I have loved you 
(John 13:34).  This love reaches out to those who cannot love, refuse to love, or don’t know how to love.  After all, when Jesus found us – we were unlovable   And while making sure we are in complete agreement to His will is sometimes a process, there’s not a time that God ever stops loving us. 

When Jesus walked on the earth, mankind was cruel to Him.  They misunderstood his teaching, deliberately turned away from His teachings, tortured Him, accused Him of wrong doings although He was innocent, and mocked Him though He came to take away the sins of the world.  After bearing the ridicule of man, He faced the punishment of God for all the bad things you and I have ever done.  If there was ANYONE who could justly stop loving us, it was Christ … yet, His love intensified all the more.  If He so loved us from eternity past, surely we can love other believers today. 

1 John 4:7, “Beloved, let us love one another: for love is of God; and every one that loveth is born of God, and knoweth God.”

title: Bitterness - A root that must be plucked out
html:
"Looking diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God; lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you, and thereby many be defiled" Hebrews 12:15
Today’s scripture passage reminds us that when we fail to live in God’s grace, we may allow a root of bitterness to establish itself in our lives.  This bitterness could be toward others, toward God, or toward the seeming judgment or punishment God may allow to come our way.  Perhaps the circumstances in life did not go the way we wanted; we avoid people or situations because the hurt feelings come back to tell us the others are completely wrong.  We fail to forgive others.  If we allow that hurt to take root in our lives, it will affect not only ourselves but it will spread like a cancer to our friends and family.

One of the reasons for bitterness is that we perceive a wrong or injustice has been done to us, or our family, or our church and we want the other person to make it right (or if they can’t make it right, admit they were wrong and feel the same pain we feel).  Such results must be left with the Lord and His dealings with His children.  We are not called to right our perceived wrongs; it is true there are many different and difficult circumstances that we could not begin to relate to.  Nonetheless, forgiven people forgive others.  As difficult as it is, God’s ways are always the same:

“ 31 Let all bitterness, and wrath, and anger, and clamour, and evil speaking, be put away from you, with all malice: 32 And be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ's sake hath forgiven you.”  Ephesians 4:31-32

title: Christlike Through Trials
html:
"2 My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations; 3 Knowing this, that the trying of your faith worketh patience.  4 But let patience have her perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing."  James 1:2-4
Another reason why we need to go through the fires of temptations and testing is to develop a Christ like spirit!  This is the meaning behind being “entire”; all Christians need to reflect the love and character of their Savior!  Discipleship means picking up our cross daily and following after Him; it may seem a huge responsibility to become what the Bible calls a “living sacrifice” (Romans 12:1-2); but actually, it is our reasonable service.

Being like Christ simply means acting and speaking like Jesus.  Some believe they will forever be caught in sin as a Christian for the rest of their lives.  But this is not true; we can act and live like Jesus in every area of our life every day of our life! 

But how?  What if we have put ourselves back into sin and now we are struggling every day?  How could we become “entire” meaning we are totally dedicated to the Lord?  The solution is to cry out to Him in prayer and repentance!  Begin committing yourself to living, breathing, and reading God’s word so it becomes the most essential thing necessary in the Christian life.  Be filled with the Holy Spirit of God, not with the things of this world (Ephesians 5:18-19).

Don’t go to Jesus just once; just twice; just five times.  Go back to Him daily, hourly if needed.  Submit yourself to Him, and He will give you a new heart with new desires.  Soon, you will think His thoughts and act out His ways so you too will be wholly sanctified to Him.  Then, you will have a strong witness for Him in the world and a lasting peace that will never fade away.

title: Come to Him as a little child
html:
"6 Humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you in due time: 7 Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you." 1 Peter 5:6-7

"Verily I say unto you, Whosoever shall not receive the kingdom of God as a little child, he shall not enter therein." Mark 10:15
There are so many cares in the world; equally, there is so much pride. As we learned in our last blog post, those who follow the path of pride are resisted by God, and those who follow the path of humility are given grace. (James 4:6)

With so many cares in the world, you would think we would pray more often for His provisions. Elders on social security are getting less and less; medicare doesn't cover even basic needs; government healthcare was rolled out with tons of problems; the price of gas, food, and basic clothing is sometimes not affordable to the hardest working people, either here or around the world. 

Many godly, wonderful people are attempting to solve these issues for their fellow human beings. Many more people have taken the problems into their own hands and have forgotten to include God. It is pride that says, “I know better than God, I can solve these problems on my own.” Just because our problems are not solved as fast as we would like it to be solved does not give us the right to solve them on our own. While we probably won’t open the front door and find boxes of food or a stash of money, the Lord may strengthen us to get a second job, provide extra help from unexpected sources, or provide for a miracle.

How do we know if we are trusting the Lord to take care of all our needs? Observe a toddler. What can the toddler do to get food? Nothing; they must wait to be fed from their parents. How can they change their diaper or get new clothes for the day? They must wait for their parents to take care of them. Jesus said something similar about how we must come to Him. You must come to God as a little child (Mark 10:15).

In the eyes of God, are you a little child?

title: Diligence in an Age of Instant
html:
"14 Follow peace with all men, and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord: 15 Looking diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God; lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you, and thereby many be defiled"  Hebrews 12:14
In order to remember and take hold of God’s grace, we need a dose of old fashioned diligence.  It is not bad to have cell phones, ipods, and kindles; but all this technology sometimes gives us a false sense of accomplishment.  Its ‘instant’ nature may also make it hard to discipline ourselves.  However, in God’s kingdom – it takes discipline and diligence to following God’s path.  We must continually strive, even when our flesh becomes tired and no longer wants to read God’s word or pray.

What do we do then?  We rely on God’s grace.  Just like the Apostle Paul asked for healing from one of his infirmities, God’s response was, “My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness.” (2 Corinthians 12:9)

When we become tired, even exhausted – God’s grace is available in such abundance that it will take over in our lives and see us through difficult times.  If we feel weak or we feel as if we are straying off the narrow path of holiness, God’s grace (His goodness and gifts of love on us) will allow us to say as Paul, “Most gladly therefore will I rather glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me.” (2 Corinthians 12:9)

Our brain is a magnificent gift from the LORD that was affected by sin in the garden of Eden.  We need to daily renew our mind with the Bible so that overtime, it will no longer be a struggle for us to love God.  Very soon, a new habit will form that will say no to sin and yes to God.  Solomon wrote it this way:  "Keep thy heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life."  (Proverbs 4:23)

title: Do you want God's wisdom?
html:
“This wisdom descendeth not from above, but is earthly, sensual, devilish. For where envying and strife is, there is confusion and every evil work.” James 3:15-16 KJV
The difference between the wisdom of man and the wisdom of God is simply amazing. God's wisdom does not cause us to do wrong or hurt other people.  God's wisdom holds us together.  On the other hand, following the wisdom of common, contemporary thinking leads us away from our loving Father. In some instances, worldly wisdom may cause us to want to get angry with people every time they don't agree with us; then we wonder why there is confusion and hurt. 

If you realize you are following the wisdom of the world in your life and you want to change - what type of wisdom should we have? 
James 3:15 informs us that we should seek the wisdom from above which means to seek wisdom from God. Let us run into the loving arms of Jesus Christ.

But how do we know if we are on the right track of finding this wisdom? We know because it is pure, merciful, and peaceful.  Someone who has God's wisdom will admit when they are wrong to their friends and ask Christ to show them the right way to live.  This wisdom will also help us to see that we aren't born perfect, but we can learn how to sin less by being God's friend! All this was made possible because God sent His only Son to die for our sins on the cross.  Do you know Jesus Christ as your personal Savior?

Do you see the difference between following God and following the world?  If we follow people and their ways, we tend to stop loving God and may even build resentful feelings to our fellow man.  But when we following after Him, God's peace will comfort us in times of trouble and bring a quiet spirit into our lives; we will fall in love with Him in all humility.  O, the joys of a life given over to God!  Do you have this life today?

title: Don’t Go Back to the Old Way
html:
"For it is not possible that the blood of bulls and of goats should take away sins."  Hebrews 10:4
Hebrews is a wonderful book of the Bible that teaches Jewish Christians as well as Gentile believers today that we do not want to go back to the old way.  Before Christ came to earth, the Jews had focused their attention on works, performing sacrifices, and conducting celebrations in hopes of going to heaven.  While some Jews realized they could only live by faith, others were trusting in their works to obtain God.  When Christ walked among the Jews, He eliminated the sacrifices and celebrations the Jews had so long after sought.  He became the final sacrifice when He died for our sins and, in fact, “resisted unto blood, striving against sin.” (Hebrews 12:4)  After all, the blood of bulls and goats (or any other man made way) can not take away sin.
Many people today are discovering anew that there is no certain Sunday, no certain devotion, and no certain man centered work they could do to receive the complete and total forgiveness of their sins.  Only Christ in His finished work at the cross can save us.  Even after they have discovered how to be born again [click here for more information], they sometimes slip back into the older patterns of a “works gospel”.  It is similar to when the Israelites crossed the Red Sea after being delivered from the taskmasters of Egypt:  they complained and wished to be in Egypt again (Exodus 16:13)!

Have you gone back to the ways of sin or are you trying to please God based only on whatever works you or your denomination can come up with?  Or are you living in the freedom of Christ, obeying His word, and seeking after a life that would please him?  Listen to the sermon below and learn how to remember the Lord and His ways!

title: Faith, Light, and Life!
html:
"3 We give thanks to God and the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, praying always for you, 4 Since we heard of your faith in Christ Jesus, and of the love which ye have to all the saints" 
Colossians 1:3-4
Todays' scriptures point out that we can rejoice in our faith not because we believe in anything, but because we believe in Christ! 

Everybody wants to have faith in something or someone who is bigger than themselves, even if it is the ideal person they wish to be.  Atheists and agnostics are forced to have faith in themselves or in humanity as a whole.  There is an innate desire inside all of us to believe in something.

True faith is a faith in Jesus, He who was crucified for our sins and risen to give us new life.  According to verse 12, before we have faith in Him, we lived in darkness.  Funny thing about spiritual darkness:  we don’t know we live in this spiritual darkness until Christ turns the light on.  It’s like the man who was born blind and does not know what it means to see; when we have faith only in ourselves or in other people, we continue to walk in blind darkness because we all have disobeyed God’s law.  Because we are all born in sin, we are all born into darkness and we are all under the power of the prince of darkness. 

Nonetheless, for those who have believed on Christ as their only Savior, Jesus has delivered them out of darkness and delivered them into the light of Christ. (1 Peter 2:9) Rejoice, oh Christian, that we walk in the light of Him who is the Prince of Life.  Charles Wesley wrote it this way in an older hymn:

Long my imprisoned spirit lay,
Fast bound in sin and nature’s night;
Thine eye diffused a quickening ray,
I woke, the dungeon flamed with light.
My chains fell off, my heart was free,
I rose went forth, and followed Thee!
Amazing love, how can it be that Thou my God shouldst die for me?

Have you never experienced Christ awakening your heart to the reality of who He is, the only one who can save us from sin, self, and the devil?  Click here to learn more about eternal life.

title: Faith Like a Chair
html:
"12 Giving thanks unto the Father, which hath made us meet to be partakers of the inheritance of the saints in light: 13 Who hath delivered us from the power of darkness, and hath translated us into the kingdom of his dear Son: 14 In whom we have redemption through his blood, even the forgiveness of sins" Colossians 1:12-14
Why is there only one way of salvation through faith, and one way to receive the forgiveness of sins?  How is it like sitting in a chair?  Read on.  

Our text today says that Christians have received the forgiveness of sin.  Why doesn’t the Lord allow those who have done good works to get into heaven?  Very often, we know people are still relying on their works if someone asks them why God should let them into heaven, and they say, “I’ve been good; I’ve never done bad things like Hitler or Stalin.  I’ve never told big lies or stolen anything of importance, so God has to let me in.  Right?”

Wrong!  Who determines the standard of how good is good enough to enter heaven?  Who came up with the rule that we need to be perfect to enter heaven?  God did.  What do the scriptures say about our innate goodness?  That we have none.  “There is none righteous, no not one.”  Romans 3:10.  If heaven is where God lives, who says He is not allowed to make the rules for those who can live there?

The VFW tells us only veterans of foreign wars can gain membership; there are many other clubs where admittance is granted only under certain conditions.  We follow those rules and conditions; does not the same principle apply to the Lord?

Membership to heaven is gained by those whose sins have been completely forgiven.  You don’t have to wait until the First Sunday after Easter either to receive it!  And once you have it, you will never lose eternal life. How can you receive this forgiveness of sin?

Think of a chair; you sit in it and put your full weight into it and have faith that it will hold you up.  So too, you must completely believe that only Jesus Christ is capable and sufficient to die for your sins, forgive your sins, and give you a new heart to follow Him!  Another hymnist wrote it this way:  "Nothing in my hand I bring.  Simply to the cross I cling”  Put your full weight on Jesus; be saved today!  Learn more here.

title: Follow the Right Path:  Rejoice, Do Not Sulk
html:
"Wherefore lift up the hands which hang down, and the feeble knees;"  Hebrews 12:12
Even in the suffering of Christ on the cross, the Scriptures say there was a ‘joy’ that was set before Him because He was obeying God (Hebrews 12:2).  In Hebrews 12, we are told that God may chastise us because of our sins.  However, being disciplined by God is a proof that God loves us and wants to develop the character of godliness inside of us; therefore, the writer of Hebrews encourages us to “lift up the hands which hang down, and the feeble knees” (verse 12) which, in our modern day English, means – stop being downtrodden and find the joy that comes about from God’s faithful discipline in our life.
Don’t fail God’s grace by letting bitterness rise up inside of you (verse 15).  Often time, believers follow after God, perform the right deeds, and pray exceedingly hard to be close with Him.  However, sin creeps in either purposefully or accidently; it takes us out of fellowship with Jesus.  In His loving kindness, God disciplines us through various means.  We realize we are guilty, we repent of our sins, and God closes the case and restores our fellowship with Him.  What is our response as human beings?  We are still sorry!  We berate ourselves, feel sorry for ourselves, and continue to beat ourselves with the guilt over our sins.  

Let’s not sulk!  Let’s rise back up in God’s forgiveness and go forward in the kingdom of God.  The Psalmist says it this way:  

“Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why art thou disquieted in me? hope thou in God: for I shall yet praise him for the help of his countenance. (Psalm 42:5)”

title: God's forgiveness for those who confess
html:
"If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness." - 1 John 1:9
     Is there any hope for those who, after having accepted Christ as Lord and Savior, have fallen back into sin? No sin is too small or too big that it does not need forgiveness. Perhaps you were rude to a clerk at the store; maybe you told a little ‘white lie’; or maybe you have a sinful habit like looking with lust toward others either in the movies or on your computer. The reality is that sometimes Christians may still sin; even though John says our spirits can never sin (1 John 5:18), if we are not careful - we can sometimes walk back in darkness. What hope do we have?

     First, realize that disobeying God is not inevitable. This verse does not say “when we confess our sin”, but “IF we confess our sin”. As a child of God, we should not go looking for sin or assume that we can’t help but fall every now and then. This verse is not a license to do wrong, but rather a help for those who are truly struggling to be godly in this evil world.

     Second, we ought to know we are not alone in fighting the flesh. Sin affects all of us in different ways. As we strive for the holiness that Christ Jesus has asked of us - you may catch the attention of the evil one who will do all he can to place enticing, worldly pleasures before you. But understand we are all struggling with our sin nature and the way to overcome it is to choose not to be conformed to this world, but rather to be transformed by the renewing of our mind by reading the Bible! (Romans 12:1-2) 

     Third, confess your sins to God and God alone. No one, not a priest, a pastor, a parent, a friend, or a spouse can act as a mediator and forgive your sins. Only Jesus can forgive your sins, but you must first confess each one of them to Him. To confess means to acknowledge we have done wrong according to God’s word and recognize we may have hurt people along the way. When we agree with God that we have done wrong, He forgives us and cleanses us! Hallelujah!

title: God's good and perfect gifts!
html:
James 1:17 - "17 Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and cometh down from the Father of lights, with whom is no variableness, neither shadow of turning."
There are many gifts that our heavenly Father might give to us on a daily basis; but for those who are walking in a relationship with Christ, we need the gift of overcoming sin and living in holiness.  Consider God's goodness to us:  remembering God's goodness will keep us from sin.

All good gifts come from God above; we know these presents are from Him because they are good, they give Him glory, and they help draw us away from the world and closer to Him.  

Nonetheless, many Christians today have gone to the water holes of sin looking for these good gifts; Jesus cannot be found there.  It is Satan's desire that we become deceived into believing that the world, the flesh, or the devil can give us the good and fulfilling things we need.  The point is to make us ineffective Christians with stunted growth.

Now, take a deep breath!  And exhale.  The very air you breathe is God's gift to us; there are many things we have that others may not have either in this country or around the world.  The fact you are reading this shows you have some sort of access to computers and machinery to learn more about God and the Bible.  Instead of looking at what we don't have, let's look at what we do have and praise God for it!

But, why do we still sometimes go to the world for what only God can give us?  Find out and listen to the complete sermon below:

title: God's Grace Offered Forgiveness before we asked for it.
html:
8 For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God ... Ephesians 2:8
God’s grace is amazing; He is known as the “God of all grace” [1 Peter 5:10] in the Holy Bible.  When we think of God, do we think of how longsuffering and kind He is?  We have disobeyed His holy laws (the very heart of God), we have thrown our fist up before Him, and we have tried to define our own righteousness rather than relying on His righteousness and His ways.  Even as believers in Him, we often fail to be as gracious and kind as He is to us.
One day, a mother of two ran upstairs in her children’s room to find out why her older eight year old was screaming so loudly.  She discovered the two year daughter was pulling on his hair; the mother assured the young man that his little sister didn’t mean to do that.  “She doesn’t know pulling hair hurts so much” she informed him.   Once she stopped her from pulling his hair, the mother believed she had resolved the situation.  But only a few moments later, she returned when she heard a shriek from her daughter.  She found her son had been pulling on her daughter’s hair; he said satisfied, “Well, now she knows what it feels like!”

The truth is, when we are hurt by someone else – we want that other person to know the pain we felt; this often causes us to retaliate in revenge, to speak badly about the other person, and to even reject the other person so that we would never talk to them.  We wait for them to ask us forgiveness; but Jesus didn’t wait, He went straight to the cross to make salvation available for all of us.

So this week, remember that our sins hurt God.  Instead of retaliating, instead of trying to harm us, the LORD Jesus died on the cross, paid the penalty for our sins, and offers forgiveness to us freely.  If we don’t know Him as Savior, we must receive His forgiveness by repentance and faith.  If we do know Christ as our Lord, we must forgive others just as He has forgiven us.  That is … grace; God’s Riches at Christ’s Expense.

title: God's Grace:  Receiving what you need, not always what you want
html:
"And he said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness."  2 Corinthians 12:9
God’s grace is His goodness, His direction, His guidance, and His watch care for His children.  His grace helps us stop sinning, induces joy, lifts us up in difficult moments, and leads us along His path.  Someone once said that grace is “God’s Riches At Christ’s Expense”.  

God’s grace also gives us everything we need, not necessarily everything we want.  For example, the Apostle Paul asked the Lord to remove the thorn in his flesh that had been plaguing him for a long time.  In fact, Paul states, “For this thing I besought the Lord thrice, that it might depart from me.” (2 Corinthians 12:8)  Three times Paul asked; yet, this was God’s response:  “My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness.”  (2 Corinthians 12:9). 

In other words – Paul thought he needed healing, but the Lord knew he needed grace.  Think about the one thing you have desired to have all your life, that dream you are holding on to, or that infirmity you are having a hard time bearing.  Ask yourself:  would my life be better if I had what I wanted, but did not have God’s grace?  Sometimes, God answers “no” to our prayer requests for one simple reason:  He has something much better for us!  Do not fail God’s grace; accept it with gladness.  Even though God did not take away Paul’s infirmity, Paul continued to lead others to Jesus and, in fact, he learned how to take pleasure in his distresses.  Moreover, Paul now could say, “When I am weak, then am I strong.” (2 Corinthians 12:10)

Let God’s grace work through you today; look for God’s grace in your own weaknesses.  In this way, you will give Him all the glory!

title: James 4 - Grace Overcoming Complacency
html:
Watch your prayer life; observe the requests you have of God, why you are Him asking for it, and what items (if any) you are thanking Him for.  The answers to these questions can help determine if you are desiring God’s heart, or have you become complacent.  We can become complacent on spiritual matters because our focus is on our flesh’s goal; James tells us we can desire for things we cannot obtain.  Perhaps we turn to God as a way to fulfill our fleshly wishes, but alas – “ye ask amiss, that ye may consume it upon your lusts.”  (James 4:2-3)
Just like we wash our physical bodies regularly, we need to regularly experience personal revival.  But how can we stop asking “amiss”?  Before asking the Lord for anything, let’s check with Him on whether what we want is really His desire for our lives.  Let’s stop trying to be independent, building our own kingdom, or getting jealous of the gifts other have.  In fact, let’s really seek God’s face in all of our matters so we can accept His grace to either fulfill His desires or be content with what He has given us already.   Maybe it is as simple as just remembering God, not just the gifts He gives.

Want to learn more about how to Grow in Grace and overcome complacency?  Please consider subscribing to this blog to the left and/or listen to the whole sermon below.  God Bless you.
"Ye ask, and receive not, because ye ask amiss, that ye may consume itupon your lusts."  James 4:3

title: James 4 - Grace Overcoming Our Unfaithfulness
html:
Consider who our faithful, true Friend is so we do not become the spiritual adulterers James speaks of in James 4:4.When Jesus walked among the earth before His resurrection, He compared His love for us to a Jewish wedding, often 
comparing Himself as the bridegroom and we, as all believers, the bride.  When a man and woman fell in love, they would become “betrothed”, which was as legal as the marriage covenant though they would not live together until after the wedding ceremony.  The husband would prepare a room or house where he could live with his beloved; only his father would know when it was ready.  If someone ever asked the groom – “When will you and your betrothed get married”, the bridegroom could literally answer, “But of that day and hour knoweth no man … but my Father only.” (Matthew 24:36)  When the groom’s father said it was time, the husband would come unannounced to take his beloved to himself for the rest of his life.  


Consider how Jesus has done the same; He gave His life as a ransom for many.  He went to Heaven to prepare a place for us (John 14:1-3), and he has given us His Holy Spirit.  He is physically returning at the appointed time to receive to Himself the Bride (that’s us) whom He loves so much.  Knowing all of this, why would we turn to anything or anyone else other than Christ for our deepest needs?  Be faithful to He who is faithful to you.

Do you know Jesus Christ as your personal Savior?  Please click here to learn more about eternity.  Consider subscribing to our blog through email on the right hand sidebar and/or listening to the entire sermon below.  Grow in grace! 

4 Ye adulterers and adulteresses, know ye not that the friendship of the world is enmity with God? whosoever therefore will be a friend of the world is the enemy of God. 5 Do ye think that the scripture saith in vain, The spirit that dwelleth in us lusteth to envy? 6 But he giveth more grace. Wherefore he saith, God resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble.  James 4:4-6

title: James 4:1-6 - Grace Overcoming Strife
html:
When Mom asked her son why he was covered with so much dirt so early in the morning, the son replied, “I went to bed that way!”  
So too, many Christians live day to day never dealing with the many problems of their past.  Believers in the Bible had similar struggles; for instance, James points out in chapter 4 many “fightings” and “wars” (v. 1) which came about because they obsessed over wayward desires (or lust for any person, place, or prominence).  Any time we are willing to forsake loving God or serving others so we can fulfill a selfish desire, we will cause wars and fighting with the flesh.  Never believe for a moment that God gives us selfish desires because … He doesn't.  (James 4:5)


The way to overcome the “lusts of the flesh” is to “walk in the Spirit” (Galatians 5:16-18).  This means to submit our wills and needs to the only One who can fulfill them.  Yup, if you are fulfilling the lusts of the flesh then you are not walking in the Spirit.  But, if you are walking in the Spirit, you will not fulfill the lusts of the flesh.  The good news:  God’s gives more grace for those who will humble themselves under His nail pierced hands!  (James 4:6)

Want to learn more about Grace that Overcomes Strife?  Keep reading this blog or listen to the entire sermon below.  Also, enjoy the old fashioned Youtube Hymn that reminds us that Jesus is always Sweeter Still.
"But he giveth more grace. Wherefore he saith, God resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble." James 4:6

title: James 4:3-6 - Grace Overcoming Selfishness
html:
While there is a place for larger ministries, Jesus often showed us that having a crowd was not as important to Him as selflessly serving individuals.  While He was leaving Jericho, the multitude that had followed Him told a blind beggar not to shout out to Jesus “have mercy on me.”  Instead of seeing blind Bartimaeus (Mark 10:46) as an impediment to His ministry, Jesus saw an individual to serve; Bartimaeus received His sight that day and became a Believer!  What would have happened if Christ had decided to ignore believing Bartimaeus?
In the walk of the believer, there are “potholes” of selfishness or, as James calls it, personal “lusts” (James 4:3-6).  Sometimes, we sap the energy the Lord has given to us to serve our sins, personal addictions, or personal comfort levels.  Maybe we fixate on gaining something we were never supposed to have in the first place and, as a result, when blind Bartimaeus calls upon us – we are found unprepared to be the hands of God's blessings.  In order for revival to occur, we need to say no to “self” and say yes to showing mercy to others.  After all, Jesus said “Be ye therefore merciful, as your Father also is merciful.” (Luke 6:36)

Want to learn more about Grace that Overcomes Selfishness?  Keep reading this blog or listen to the entire sermon below. 
"Ye ask, and receive not, because ye ask amiss, that ye may consume it upon your lusts."  James 4:3

title: Jesus Is Enough
html:
2 My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations; 3 Knowing this, that the trying of your faith worketh patience.  4 But let patience have her perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing.  James 1:2-4
A pastor was once in downtown Cincinnati when a man came up and asked him for a drink.  He specifically asked for a “pop” or soda; the minister used this opportunity to teach his students that the man thought he wanted soda to drink, but what his body was really craving was water.  He really wanted water, but he didn't know it.

Since the garden of Eden, we have been separated from the Lord.  Adam and Eve deliberately sinned, and our nature is such that we deliberately fall away from God.  We don’t wish to follow Him.

Yet, our social experiment of living life without God is an ABSOLUTE FAILURE!  We are always in “want”; we are always craving something.  Why are there so many who love something more than God be it their job, family, sex, drugs, music, or even innocuous  things like relationships or friendships?  Because they are craving God but don’t know it.

Even born again Christians are going back to the dirty waters of sin hoping to find lasting satisfaction; we want a quick fix for our life.  We want to be forgiven and just live happily ever after.  But the truth is, the temptations and trials that cause us difficulties are there to help us to we rely more and more on Christ and then we can say we are “wanting nothing”.  With Christ, there are no endless cravings and nothing else in creation can satisfy us like He does.  As we fill our spiritual cup with His friendship, we realize that being being entire and wanting nothing is the perfect work of maturity.


Crying out to God when we are saved is just the beginning; as Christians, we must cry out to Him daily and seek His face.  Let the Scriptures fill your mind and heart; soon you will see that the things this world has to offer is a garbage can compared to what Christ gives us as we walk with God.  To know Him, enjoy Him, and love Him is our aim; before we can do any sort of service for God - we must "get happy in Him!"  How do we know when He has become our all in all?  Simply because your heart proclaims in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs - "Jesus is enough".

Consider this Psalm:

The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.  He maketh me to lie down in green pastures: he leadeth me beside the still waters.  Psalm 23:1-2.

If you are in the area or in need of a church home, please consider joining us this Sunday as we worship the Lord and continue in our studies of the epistle of James.

title: John 19 - The King of Kings Who Loved to be a Servant
html:
"5 Let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus: 6 Who, being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God: 7 But made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant, and was made in the likeness of men: 8 And being found in fashion as a man, he humbled himself, and became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross."  Philippians 2:5-8
If you were tried based on false accusations, condemned based on phony court proceedings, and spit upon and mocked even though all you ever did was help other people – you would have something to complain about.  The scales of justice would be turned the wrong way, and you would do everything you could to right what was wrong.

All of this happened to Jesus; yet, before anything else – He thought of the needs of others.  Could it be that the purest Son of God willingly hung on the cross, being punished by his Father for the sins of the world, because we were in such a damnable state? Graham Kendrick’s song says, “My Lord, what love is this, That pays so dearly? That I, the guilty one, May go free!” 

What was Jesus’s secret?  Paul says he “took upon him the form of a servant” and “he humbled himself’.  (Philippians 2)  The sinless Lamb of God who could, at any time, call an army of angels to rescue Him instead was willingly crushed on the cross so we could enter into a relationship with Him. 

It is not that Jesus never thought of himself;  false humility claims we never think of ourselves.  Jesus’s humility was genuine; He thought of others before He thought about Himself.

We are called to serve Jesus; we are called to serve others; then we are called to take care of ourselves – in that order.  Let’s wash one another’s feet and lay down our lives for each other.

Learn more about what the sinless Son of God did on the cross; listen to the complete sermon below!

title: John 19:25-27 – Disciples of Jesus are always Available
html:
"25 Now there stood by the cross of Jesus his mother, and his mother's sister, Mary the wife of Cleophas, and Mary Magdalene. 26 When Jesus therefore saw his mother, and the disciple standing by, whom he loved, he saith unto his mother, Woman, behold thy son! 27 Then saith he to the disciple, Behold thy mother! And from that hour that disciple took her unto his own home."  John 19:25-27
Lessons on Duty:  The account of Jesus entrusting the care of His earthly mother to John teaches us the importance of having an open and ready heart anytime Jesus calls upon us.  John was ready and available to be used of the Lord; perhaps some would have understood if John only stood there and mourned.  Instead, He readily obeyed and served His Lord even nigh death’s door.

Disciples of Jesus are available.  Our marching orders are coming from the Lord Jesus; for John, He was on the cross.  For us, He is now in heaven, wanting us to show others that same cross!  All through history, God has had his servants who obeyed Him and not the world or religious institutions.  Ananias helped Saul (who later became Paul) when he was blinded by the light of Christ (Acts 9:10).  Ananias said to the Lord, “Behold, I am here, Lord.”  Even in the Old Testament, when God went looking for volunteers, Isaiah said, “Here am I, send me.” (Isaiah 6:8)  Now, He wants to send you.

Is your heart available to Him now?  We need to cultivate a serving heart now; it is not enough to sing “I surrender all”; we must surrender all.  The Master is waiting to use you, but He may call at any time without notice.  We want to serve Him with our whole heart; wherever God has called you and whatever lot in life you find yourself – if you are a disciple of Christ, always be at attention.  Peter says it this way:  “be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear” (1 Peter 3:15)

Hark!  The Master is calling! Listen to the whole sermon below.

title: John 19:25-27 – Disciples of Jesus are willing to Change
html:
"26 When Jesus therefore saw his mother, and the disciple standing by, whom he loved, he saith unto his mother, Woman, behold thy son! 27 Then saith he to the disciple, Behold thy mother! And from that hour that disciple took her unto his own home."  John 19:25-27
Set in our ways:  Because it is comfortable, it is often more preferable for us to remain where we are.  Being set in our ways may have some experience and wisdom behind it, but normally – our ministry and service does not stay the same forever.  God wants us to be willing to change our attitude, direction, focus, and plans.  

John receiving Mary into his home by order of Jesus would have been an incredibly big change.  Another example of change as when the Apostle Paul and Silas desired to go into Asia (Acts 16:6-10), but the Holy Spirit would not allow them.  Instead, He directed them to start churches in Macedonia.  How many lost souls would continue to be lost if they did not obey the Spirit of God?  How many blessings have we lost for our refusal to obey Him even though it meant changing what we were comfortable with?

Right response:  Our right response to God is obedience; don’t become depressed.  That does neither God or ourselves any good.  It is okay to be nervous; God is unable to use prideful people.  But it is not okay to say no to His will.  We should not change simply because it is novel or different; we should change because Jesus is calling us to do a deeper work for him.

Consider joining us for worship this Lord’s Day, Sunday March 10, 2013, at Berkshire Hills Baptist Church in Lee, MA!

title: John 19:26-27 – Disciples of Jesus are Willing
html:
"26 When Jesus therefore saw his mother, and the disciple standing by, whom he loved, he saith unto his mother, Woman, behold thy son! 27 Then saith he to the disciple, Behold thy mother! And from that hour that disciple took her unto his own home." John 19:26-27
Being ready and trustworthy are great characteristics that can be negated if you are not willing to serve Jesus.  He was willing to go to the cross for us, shed His blood, pay for our sins, and rise from the grave.  Surely, we would be willing to spread this good news to the ends of the earth.

But perhaps we are afraid that the Lord will send us somewhere that is hard or difficult.  Maybe we become like Moses when first asked to serve and we make many excuses (Exodus 4); Lord, I’m not educated; Lord, I don’t speak well; Lord, I’m too old; Lord, the place you want me to go is too far away.

Don’t you think the Lord is fully aware of your limitations; if He is asking you to go, don’t you think He will enable you to be sent?  All He is asking for us is to be willing to go.  Look at John in our Bible passage today.  He was ready and available at the foot of the cross; the moment Jesus gave Mary into his care, John immediately took Mary into his own household to care for her.  He obeyed his master, even in the most dire of circumstances.  Won’t you stop making excuses today, and serve Him when He has called you?

There is something else that is commendable in John’s actions; His decision to obey and take Mary as his own mother showed a very important characteristic of his heart; want to know what it is?  Listen to the whole sermon below or look out for the next blog entry in two days!

title: Steadfast Christians Lost in Their Love for Him
html:
"And they continued stedfastly in the apostles' doctrine and fellowship, and in breaking of bread, and in prayers."  Acts 2:42
Acts 2:42 tells us that the early Christians were steadfast in three things:  * the Apostle’s doctrine, *fellowship, * the Lord’s table, and * prayers.  In other words, the early Christians had a faith which was more than just believing in Him; they were diligent in the disciplines that God had taught them.  They didn’t just “amen” the preacher to death on Sunday only to live like the wicked world on Monday!  Their testimony helped to bear witness to the truth of Jesus in the world.

What kind of decisions do we make in front of unbelievers?  What kind of life do we live when no one else watching us?  What kind of life will leave a lasting impression? 

Steadfast in the Apostle’s Doctrine:  Worldly philosophy is not lasting; but the teachings of the Apostles, namely the Holy Scriptures – that will last for all eternity.  We can be sure that what He says in His word is true today, tomorrow, and forever.  Having a written English Bible to help us in God’s way is great – we don’t have to guess at what God wants to tell us!  

Steadfast in Fellowship:  In Acts 2:9, we learn that the church of God is made up of people from various ethnicities.  No one people group are better or worse than anyone; in fact, for all those that call upon Christ for salvation, we are one.  Our diverse backgrounds serve as celebration that Jesus’s death on the Cross was for all men!  Even more - in heaven, we will be one and we will no longer fight with each other over denominations or beliefs.  Galatians 3:28 points out, “There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male or female:  for ye are all one in Christ Jesus.” 

Go find a local bible believing church to serve in!  Every church needs a few good women and men to serve. 

Consider visiting us if you are in the area.

Listen to the complete sermon:

07.28.13 A Rewarding Grace - mp3link

title: Lord – Lead Us Not Into Temptation, Lead us into You.
html:
“Blessed is the man that endureth temptation:  for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life, which the Lord hath promised to them that love him.”  James 1:12 
We can fall into our own pity parties in the trials that we go through; whether they be testings from God, from Satan, or maybe even our own silly mistakes – we humans seem to love to complain about the woes that are ailing us.  We are not the only ones going through trials; and our trials are not unique to the human race.  We must be vigilant in not falling into these pitfalls that James 1 warns us about:

1. We might blame God for our own sin.  We might try to blame God for the times when we have sinned or failed.  We can never blame God or say He led us into sin.  We must not try to shift responsibility to God for our failures; instead, we must learn our own weaknesses and make sure that under times of stress, we do not have access to those things that so easily trip us up.  “Let no man say when he is tempted, I am tempted of God:  for God cannot be tempted with evil, neither tempeth he any man” (James 1:13)

2. We might stay down for the ten count of defeat.  The nature of trials and temptations are such that we might fall into discouragement or sin; but we shouldn't stay in our sins for a count out!  If you have fallen and you want to get back up again -  call upon the LORD, confess your sins – and He with faithfully forgive them and heal you!  (1 John 1:9)  

Don’t blame God because you have failed to follow perfectly after Him; but if you do fall – run to Him and He will abundantly pardon!


Listen to the whole sermon below:


08.11.2013 - The Truth About Temptations - mp3link

title: Lord, you want me to do what?
html:
"And it shall be, that thou shalt drink of the brook; and I have commanded the ravens to feed thee there"  1 Kings 17:4
There was once a prophet of God who was asked to believe some pretty weird things; the Lord asked Elijah to speak out about the ungodly life style of some of the rulers of the day.  In so doing, the Lord used Elijah to prophesy about a drought in Israel.  As a result, God told Elijah that He would take care of Him even though there would be no food or water.  Elijah was sent to a brook to wait on the Lord, and there – he was told (1 Kings 17:3) that he would drink from the nearby brook and be fed by birds (ravens) who would come by every so often to feed him!  Would you wait at a brook and wait for food from the mouth of birds?  It would take faith.

As we walk in the journey of faith, we sometimes pray and ask the Lord to help us with our needs.  In our thoughts, we have in mind exactly how God will provide.  But the Lord knows best how to take care of His children, and sometimes He meets our needs in the most unexpected ways.  Instead of giving extra money for food, maybe He simply gives us a sack of groceries from a good Samaritan.  Or maybe He doesn’t quite give us the job we want so we can bless someone else’s life who needs it.  Whatever the case, He knows exactly what are our needs are even before we think about it.  So put your trust in Him and expect the unexpected; God never forsakes those who believe in His Son! 

The river that Elijah was sitting by, however, dried up (1 Kings 17:7).  Would God still be able to provide for Elijah, the prophet, even though all the water was now gone and there was no rain in sight?  To find out, listen to the entire sermon below!
