title: Luke 17:3-4 – Overcoming the Problems of Forgiveness, Part 1
html:
" 3 Take heed to yourselves: If thy brother trespass against thee, rebuke him; and if he repent, forgive him. 4 And if he trespass against thee seven times in a day, and seven times in a day turn again to thee, saying, I repent; thou shalt forgive him."  Luke 17:3-4
While some do not forgive others because they have not yet received Christ as their Savior and they have yet to be forgiven themselves, many do not forgive because they simply haven’t been taught how to handle the issue of an unwilling or unrepentant offender.

First of all, if a person is constantly sinning against you (hurting or bad mouthing you), Jesus advises us to continue to forgive them.  (Luke 17:3-4)  That does not mean you can’t try to help your friend to overcome repetitious sin or that you will always place yourself in the same position where you always get hurt; but it does mean that you restore the relationship.  How many times has Christ forgiven you for the same sins against Him?  Out of all the times you have asked to be forgiven from Christ, did He ever disown you?

Secondly, what happens if you extend the hand of forgiveness, but the other person does not care, does not want to apologize, or can’t seem to understand the hurt they did to you?  Realize, you did what God expects of you and there is nothing more for you to do except pray.  From a reading of the Sermon on the Mount (Matthew 5:21-26), God expects both the offended and the offender to quickly reconcile.  You have done your part; know that Christ did His part, and not everyone accepts His forgiveness.

Finally, what if someone asks forgiveness of you – yet you refuse to forgive them?  Jesus talked about this situation as well.  Do you know what He said?  To find out, subscribe to our blog and look for our next posting in two days.  Or, go ahead … listen to this scripture filled sermon below and receive the information ahead of time.  Either way, remember:  Forgiven people forgive.

title: Luke 22:54 - Prayer - A Bridge to God's Heart
html:
The day continued to get darker; not only had Jesus struggled in prayer the entire evening, His enemies captured Him with weapons in the dead of night.  Now with Christ under the arrest of the Romans, Peter had to come to grasps with the fact that His Lord had been detained and all the disciples had fled.  Oh, how distant God must have seemed to Peter.  What else should he have done but bring all his concerns to God in prayer?

The difficulty was, Peter let the problems take his eyes off of the Lord.  There is no instance that Peter checked with God in the situation; instead, he sat by the fire and lied about who he was!  Let’s not beat up on Peter, we would probably have done the same.

If we are not careful, we will distance ourselves from God, from the fellowship of other Christians, and from the Bible.  All because something happened in our life that we don’t agree with.  How sad when that happens to us; when we start to fall away from the Lord, we must immediately talk to Him.  We must begin cultivating a thankful heart (1 Thessalonians 5:18), humble ourselves before the Lord, and become teachable.  He will show us the right direction when we are in a fix; it will be the direction that is just right for us. 

If you sense the distance between God and you, bridge it with prayer.  Not sure how to pray?  Just start talking to God; there is no right way to pray.  And there is no wrong way to pray … except not to pray at all. 

(Hear the full sermon below.)
"Pray without ceasing." 1 Thessalonians 5:17

title: Luke 22:54 - Why are you following Jesus Afar Off?
html:
While it was okay that Peter was following Jesus from afar on the night of His betrayal, it was a far cry from the “honey moon” type feelings he had for His Lord only hours before. Days previous, Peter said he would die for Jesus (Mark 14:31) and he demonstrated his commitment by cutting off the soldier’s ear who attempted to capture Him. (John 18:10) And while it was true Peter was physically walking from a distance from Jesus, we see that his "three times" denial of Christ demonstrated his heart was following from afar as well.
So, why have you, as a born again, redeemed child of God, decided to walk far away from the Lord?  Maybe it is because you are afraid He will set your heart so on fire for God, He will ask you to say or do certain things you fear doing.  Or maybe you were passionate about Jesus at one time – humming a new song about God, going to new places, and even telling others about Christ’s love.  Perhaps (either literally or figuratively) people have “slammed the door to Christ” in your face one too many times and you are now discouraged.  Were you once brave for Him, and now you are lukewarm?  Consider for a moment whether you are doing God’s will, or your own.
Please continue to read our bi-daily blog this week and learn about how God restored Peter and how God can restore you into a right relationship with Him!  Or if you have the time, listen to the complete sermon below.

"Then took they him, and led him, and brought him into the high priest's house. And Peter followed afar off."  Luke 22:54

title: Luke 23 - Thinking of others while hanging on the cross
html:
"Then said Jesus, Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do. And they parted his raiment, and cast lots." Luke 23:34
Even while hanging on the cross in payment for the sins of the world and even in the middle of the agony and suffering He was experiencing, Jesus thought about others before He thought about Himself.  Jesus thought about


His enemies:  The Roman guards, the religious leaders, and the people had rejected Christ to die on the old rugged cross; instead of divine retaliation, He asked the Father, “Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do.” [Luke 23:34]  He also thought about

His companions:  The two criminals that were crucified by his side were also important people on the Savior’s mind; while one mocked Him, the other commented that they deserved to die, but Jesus did not deserve death.  He had done nothing wrong.  To Jesus, the thief asked that Christ would remember him in the kingdom of God.   Meeting the needs of others, Jesus said, “To day shalt thou be with me in paradise.” [Luke 23:43]  Jesus also thought about

His family:  He would not allow his earthly mother to not be taken care of even after His death and resurrection; in an act of selfless love, Jesus entrusted Mary to John the apostle with the words, “Behold thy mother.” [John 19:27]

The whole world:  Ultimately, the sacrifice of Christ on the cross was the supreme commitment to pay for the sins of all the world.   He willingly felt the pains of complete separation from his Father so that He could ensure that believers would never have to feel such separation.  (Matthew 27:46)

Before Jesus thought about Himself on the cross – He thought, cared, and loved others, even going so far as to suffer for them and their sins.  Won’t you accept Him today?

Listen to the complete sermon below.

title: Luke 23:34 - Classified Ad for Free Forgiveness
html:
"Then said Jesus, Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do. And they parted his raiment, and cast lots."  Luke 23:34
An account based on a true story is told of Paco, a young Spanish man who ran away from home, estranged from his father.  Realizing the need for reconciliation with his son, the father put an ad in the Madrid city newspaper, El Liberal, which read “"Paco, meet me at the newspaper stand at noon on Sunday. All is forgiven! Love, Papa."  The father did find his son at the newspaper stand on Sunday, along with many other young men named Paco who were also looking for love and acceptance from their dad!

For Jesus, He tells us to meet Him at the Cross today, now.  There, he says, “Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do.”  In ancient days, people didn’t forgive others very often, least of all their enemies.  For Jesus to ask His Father to forgive those who crucified Him to the cross was to put into practice what He taught others to do:  “Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you.” (Matthew 5:44)

Forgiveness is a virtue, and its importance is demonstrated as Jesus’ first words from His lips when He was crucified.  God wants to show His love for us; in fact, Jesus prayed and asked His Father to forgive His enemies so we could see the loving heart of the Father for all mankind.  His forgiveness is not some general thought; the cross is His “classified” ad to us!  If we would meet Him at the cross today, ask forgiveness for all of our sins, and turn away from our old life and turn totally to Him – He says, “All is forgiven!  Love, God the Father.”  

Won’t you turn to Him today?  Listen to the whole sermon below.

title: Luke 23:34 - Why Forgiveness “seems” to Fail
html:
"Then said Jesus, Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do. And they parted his raiment, and cast lots."  Luke 23:34
Notice the forgiveness of God and Jesus in Luke 23:34; yet, it “seemed” to fail because the people around the cross, in response, “parted his raiment, and cast lots.”  Why didn’t they thank the Lord that He had forgiven them for all their wrong doings?  Because, they lacked repentance; neither their hearts or minds changed.

Adam and Eve first rebelled against God in the garden of Eden (Genesis 3); since then, all human beings have a totally depraved, sinful nature.  We do wrong because it is in our nature to disobey God's ways.  All sin separates us from God.  However, when Christ died for our sins – he actually died for the sins of all the world!  All the world, literally, is forgiven of their sins.

However, until we as humans repent and agree with God that we are sinners and that we need Christ as our Savior – there is no reconciliation.  Forgiven people can still go to hell simply because they don't agree with God that they are sinners.  Once we repent and accept Christ as our personal Savior, we are reconciled to the One who created us, and we are able to have a deep friendship with Him.

So too in your personal life; does it seem “forgiveness” failed?  Find out the missing part of the equation; do you continue to hold grudges against people or have you failed to change your ways after others have forgiven you?  It may not always be easy; ask God to remove all bitterness from you and change your heart to be like Him.  After all, Christ has forgiven us (Ephesians 4:32) – so let us be kind and tenderhearted to everyone else.


Listen to the whole sermon below.

title: Luke 23:39-43 – Grace For Anyone Desiring Paradise
html:
39 And one of the malefactors which were hanged railed on him, saying, If thou be Christ, save thyself and us.  40 But the other answering rebuked him, saying, Dost not thou fear God, seeing thou art in the same condemnation?  41 And we indeed justly; for we receive the due reward of our deeds: but this man hath done nothing amiss.  42 And he said unto Jesus, Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom.  43 And Jesus said unto him, Verily I say unto thee, Today shalt thou be with me in paradise.

Luke 23:39-43
The thief on the cross came to the end of himself; he knew he was a sinner and needed Christ to save him.

A story is told of a man who was considered a “drunk”; he was always begging for money and hardly ever worked.  He says in his own testimony that drinking would take control of him; he had a family to take care of, but instead he would bring his horse to the bar and buy everyone drinks until the horse was completely sold. Another time, instead of staying home with his wife – he drove 11 miles through a massive snow storm so he could buy his fill of whiskey.  One time, when his son was 2 years old – this alcoholic came home from a ten day drinking binge to find his son dead in his mother’s arm.  At the funeral, his wife insisted he promise never to drink again.  Two hours after his vow, he came home staggering drunk.  Could Christ save a man like this?

Absolutely; after visiting Pacific Gardens Missions and being witness to by another former alcoholic, Melvin E. Trotter met Christ and became a new creature – never to return to his former life again!  To this day, the ministry he started helps others meet Christ and overcome their life dominating addictions.  http://www.meltrotter.org/home 

If you are reading this and are in despair, know this:  it doesn’t matter what you have done, where you have gone, or how low you think you have fallen.  If you would come to Jesus, repent of your sins, and put your complete and total trust in Him – then Jesus will say to you, “thou shalt be with me in Paradise.” 

Listen to the complete sermon below:

title: Luke 23:39-43:  Paradise Now
html:
"43 And Jesus said unto him, Verily I say unto thee, Today shalt thou be with me in paradise."  Luke 23:43
Jesus informed one of the wayward criminals who was crucified next to him, “Today shalt thou be with me in paradise.” No other book but the Bible is trustworthy enough to tell us what Paradise is and how we can get there. We can be assured that we are going to Paradise today; we need not wait until right before we take our last breath that heaven will be our home.

Some people use the word Paradise to mean a place of delight where they would like to be. In the Bible, paradise was originally The Garden of Eden where Adam and Eve lived in innocence; when they disobeyed God's one and only command (Genesis 3), they lost their first paradise and were forced out of the Garden.

Then, a man by the name of Abraham believed in the one living and true God and chose to follow Him with His life; He so strongly held to God by faith (and not his own works) that when others who believed like him died, they called that Paradise a place called “Abraham's bosom.” It was the resting place of those who loved God before Christ died on the cross (Luke 16:19-31). 

After Christ died on the cross, the scriptures inform us that he freed those believers in Abraham's bosom so that all who profess faith in Him could live with God for eternity. (Ephesians 4:8)  Hallelujah! Since Christ paid for all of our sins including the thief next to him on the cross – Jesus was going to bring him to Heaven – the place where God Himself dwells. Jesus promised His very special presence to the criminal, and He promises that same presence to all who put their faith in Him.

Click here to learn how to have eternal life. 

Listen to the complete sermon below!

title: Luke 23:40-43:  From Sinner to Saint!
html:
40 But the other answering rebuked him, saying, Dost not thou fear God, seeing thou art in the same condemnation?  41 And we indeed justly; for we receive the due reward of our deeds: but this man hath done nothing amiss.  42 And he said unto Jesus, Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom.  43 And Jesus said unto him, Verily I say unto thee, Today shalt thou be with me in paradise.
Luke 23:40-43
The thief on the cross was saved the same way as Paul or Peter.  Paul murdered Christians; Peter denied Christ; both Paul and Peter needed to come to the realization of their own sinfulness, repent, and believe on Him.  Just like the thief on the cross, God is willing to save any sinner that comes to Him!

First, the thief on the cross realized he deserved his punishment; he says he was crucified “justly” (v. 41). 

Second, the thief on the cross realized Jesus was completely innocent.  He says, “this man hath done nothing amiss.”  Pilate, under whom Jesus was crucified, also attested to the innocence of Jesus (Luke 23:4).  Jesus was completely sinless; He was hanging on the cross as payment for the sins of the world.  He became sin for us so that we could receive God’s righteousness in our lives. (2 Corinthians 5:21)

Third, the thief on the cross trusted his future into the hands of Jesus.  He placed his trust in Christ as the only one who could save him in the future afterlife; the thief recognized Jesus was “King” and that Jesus had a “Kingdom”.  Jesus’ response was ‘today, thou shalt be with me in paradise’.

Friend – gaining heaven is only a few words away.  The most important decision you can make is to trust Jesus Christ as personal Lord and Savior; just like there were no works the thief could do, so too there is nothing you can do to save yourself.  Being baptized, going to church, reading the Bible, or giving money to the ministry are all commendable actions.  They cannot save anyone!  What saves us and causes us to become children of God?  Galatians 3:26, “For ye are all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus.”

Listen to the entire sermon below and consider subscribing to our bi-daily blog.

title: Luke 23:43 - Promises of Paradise are Promises of Acceptance
html:
"And Jesus said unto him, Verily I say unto thee, To day shalt thou be with me in paradise."  Luke 23:43
Jesus’ comment to the thief on the Cross that he would be with Him in paradise is actually a promise of God’s acceptance!  Because heaven is where God lives, going there means God has accepted you.

However, people are people.  They feel they must say some certain prayer or litany, go to Purgatory, recite the “Our Father” a number of times, experience soul sleep, show mercy to others – SOMETHING!  Is it really easy enough to simply turn away from our old ways and then put our entire trust in the Savior?  Is believing on Jesus really all that needs to be done?  Listen to the scriptures:  “For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.” Romans 10:13.

No matter what we do, it would never be good enough.  In fact, God is so completely sinless that all sin must be punished.  We can not be pardoned either by our own merit or by combining our merit with something else.  There needed to be one Man who would be perfect in our place, and then receive the punishment our sin justly deserves.  You ask who that may be?  Christ Jesus, it is He!  

Call upon Jesus and He will answer.  Be accepted by God; know that Heaven IS your home.  Realize, this is a decision you must make.  If we have not accepted Christ as our personal Savior, the Bible tells us we are children of wrath (Ephesians 2:3).  But God is rich in mercy as demonstrated at the cross (Ephesians 2:4).  Accept Him and He will accept you.

title: Luke 23:46 - Are These Two Myths Causing You to Not Know God?
html:
"And when Jesus had cried with a loud voice, he said, Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit: and having said thus, he gave up the ghost."  Luke 23:46
In Luke 23:46, Jesus said on the cross, "Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit: and having said thus, he gave up the ghost."  Are you also able to call God your Father?

Jesus gave up His life out of His own free will.  No one can kill God; He died because He loves you and me.  Now, He was going to give up His life and He trusted his loving Father so completely that He would give Himself into His hands.  Here at the precipice of death, Christ trusted God.  There are two big myths in regards to our Heavenly Father.

Myth #1: God, the Heavenly Father, is always angry all the time.  Some only see God as a judge that punishes all sin and is angry all the time; yet, He does not want to be a judging God, He wants to be a loving Father.  That is why He allowed us to have salvation through Christ so we could become His child.  Ask yourself - do you not trust God because of how your earthly parents may have treated you?

Myth #2:  All people are God's children.  The Bible does not teach we are all children of God; we are all the creation of God.  However, we do not become children of God until we believe on Jesus by faith.  Here is what Galatians 3:16 reads, "For ye are all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus."  Ask yourself, has believing that God is everyone's Father caused you to take Him and His salvation for granted, even making you realize you do not know Christ as Savior? Perhaps you have trusted this myth to the detriment of your own soul.


Learn all about eternal life here.


Listen to the complete sermon below.

title: Mark 16:7 - Grace Whispering Your Name
html:
Today, grace (God’s unmerited favor) is whispering your name, calling you back to God, and reminding you of the gentleness and goodness of the Lord Jesus.  While God has called out many names in the past, one of the notable ones is Mark 16:7 where the angel asks the women to specifically tell the disciples and “Peter” that Jesus was risen and that He would appear to them in Galilee.
What is significant is that Jesus did not specifically call John’s name (though he was loved) or anyone else’s name but Peter.  The last time Peter saw the Lord, the scriptures say he “wept bitterly”.  (Luke 22:62)  This weeping came about as a result of his realizing he denied Christ before other people; perhaps Peter remembered when His Lord said, “But he that denieth me before men shall be denied before the angels of God.” (Luke 12:9)  Perhaps Peter thought he had committed the unforgiveable sin; thankfully, his repentant heart was evidence that this brief lapse was NOT the end of his walk with God.

Jesus extended the hand of grace to Peter even after He was risen, and He is extending that same hand of grace to you.  Don’t be trapped in the sidelines silenced by the guilt of your conscience; confess your sins and shortcoming to Him who can fully restore you!  After all, Jesus cares for you … He calleth his own sheep by name. (John 10:3)


Listen to an inspiring sermon below; if you live in Berkshire County, MA - why not listen to us live at 10:00am Sunday School or 11:00am Morning Service this Sunday?  We're saving you a seat.  

"But go your way, tell his disciples and Peter that he goeth before you into Galilee: there shall ye see him, as he said unto you."  Mark 16:7

title: Matthew 27 – Forsaken But Not Forgotten, Part 1
html:
"Now from the sixth hour there was darkness over all the land unto the ninth hour."  Matthew 27:45
Imagine the day that Christ was crucified.  People were everywhere; the city was full because there were many pilgrims there for the Passover.  People knew Jesus was being berated, so they came out to see what the commotion was about.

For the Romans, they would look for the longest path to parade a convicted criminal all the way to the place of the skull called Golgotha, where they would crucify their victims.  They wanted as many people as possible to watch the people Rome had condemned.

All the people were watching Christ carry His cross; they also watched Simon of Cyrene carry Christ’s cross.  When they came to the place of the skull, the people watched Christ crucified for our sins – though they may not have understood what was happening.  Suddenly, at the sixth to ninth hour, the Scriptures say, “there was darkness over all the land”.  (Matthew 26:45)  The darkness was not caused because the sun stop shining; instead, it was caused because the sins of the world were being placed upon the sinless One, the Son of God, the One who had never experienced sin’s aches, pains, despair, or hurt.

He went to the cross for you and for me.  The sinless Lamb of God atoned for our sins by taking upon Himself the punishment we deserved.  Part of that punishment was being totally abandoned by God.

Being abandoned by God did not mean He was forgotten.  Can you ever be abandoned by the Father as a Christian?  What happens if you feel abandoned?  Learn more about Christ and His work on the cross in the complete sermon below.

title: Matthew 6:15 – Overcoming the Problems of Forgiveness, Part 2
html:
15 But if ye forgive not men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.  Matthew 6:15
The world’s philosophy says, forgive other people for your own benefit.  God is much wiser:  He shows us that Forgiven People Forgive.  Our motivation is not solely to forgive so we can benefit; our motivation is to forgive so others will see how loving and kind God is.  But what happens when we stubbornly decide we will not extend forgiveness to someone else?  

In Matthew 18:23-35, God tells us essentially that when we refuse to forgive others, our Heavenly Father will not forgive us.  This is not speaking about our salvation, but it is rather showing that our current relationship with Him will seem distant and cold.  He illustrates this by pointing out in a story that an earthly king had forgiven the massive debt owed to him by one of his servants.  Yet, this same servant could not forgive the much smaller amount of money owed to him by one of his friends.  Once the king learned his forgiven servant could not, himself, forgive, the king admonished him and sent him to debtor’s prison to pay the original debt.  Imagine if creditors were like that today!  Jesus summed it up this way:  “if ye forgive not men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.” (Matthew 6:15)

Have you accepted Christ as personal Lord and Savior, but there seems to be distance between you and the Heavenly Father?  Are the blessings of peace and satisfaction knowing Him seemingly running short these days?  Examine your life and see if there is anyone you have not forgiven; then, forgive them from the heart.  Jesus did not wait for his enemies to ask for forgiveness; forgive from the heart of mercy God has given you.  Restore your relationship to your friend, and to your God!

Listen to the complete message below.

title: Matthew 6:33-34 - His Priorities Our First Priority
html:
33 But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.  34 Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof.  Matthew 6:33-34
Did you personally accept Jesus Christ and start seeking his Kingdom from our last blog post?  If so, welcome to God’s family!  Continue seeking after Him and His ways.

Above all, seek the Lord; make Him a priority.  It’s the first thing we should do when we awaken; give glory and honor to Him through prayer and then seek after Him by reading a faithful Bible translation, the King James Bible.  As we make Jesus a priority, then He promises He will give to us all He has in store.

Seeking Him first means do not be anxious so much about the things of tomorrow; its worries , its heartaches, its plans, its jobs – they will come soon enough.  Sufficient are the blessings and troubles of today!

God is a God of Today; in fact, He is eternal and everlasting.  You can’t change what happened yesterday, and you have very little control over the things that will happen tomorrow.  Don’t worry about the “to do list” of Monday, or you will ruin your Sunday.  While planning on retirement is a good and worthy task in taking care of yourself and family, don’t let it consume you because we have no guarantees of tomorrow.  Enjoy today and live in the now.

How can you begin or renew your journey with Him?  Pick up your Bible and begin reading it as if your spiritual life depended on it ---> because it does!  Just like a fish needs water to live and just like humans need love to survive, so too – a Christian needs his Bible to seek after God’s heart.  For each command we come upon in the Bible, we should obey not because it is a list of do’s and don’t; we should follow God’s command because every command from the LORD is an expression of His faithful heart to us.  We want to be faithful to Him because He has been faithful to us; He will never leave you or forsake you, so don’t leave or forsake Him!


Listen to the entire sermon by clicking here.

title: Matthew 6:33-34 - What are you seeking after?  What are you looking for?
html:
33 But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.  34 Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof.
- Matthew 6:33-34
Is food, drink, clothing, or the cares of this life the only thing you worry about? [Matthew 6:25] We learn in the sermon on the Mount that the secret to living an Abundant Life is:  a) not a secret and b) not found in the temporary needs of life.  The needs of life are only an end to help us trust Him more.  Our Father in Heaven knows exactly what you need; we should trust that He will provide for what we need and not always what we want.  Let’s live the life of victory by living life the way He intended it.

Seek ye first must be our first priority!  What are we to seek?  Seek His Kingdom, learn from Jesus’s feet, and be content as a loyal citizen of His heavenly rule.  When we seek Him, we should never stop seeking!  Just like a bear that is not content with one source of food, so we should not be content with only finding God one day out of the week.  Instead, we should strive to look for Him and search for Him everyday, every moment beginning with the time we arise in the morning.

Seek ye:  This implies that it is a personal seeking; while your parent’s faith might have been good enough for your parents, it won’t get you to heaven.  While there are many books, many journals, even many blogs like our own that show you God’s ways – they are not enough to fulfill the longing in your soul.  You must go to God and get saved!  You must personally accept Christ as your Savior and Lord and then follow His ways; seek ye implies personal decisions for following Him must be made today.

Why put off following Jesus?  Seek Him today while He may be found. 

Click here to learn about the gospel!

title: Maturity Through Temptation
html:
"2 My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations; 3 Knowing this, that the trying of your faith worketh patience.  4 But let patience have her perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing."  - James 1:2-4

There are many trials and testings (temptations) that come our way as Christians; our Scripture today implores us to have joy in those testings.  These temptations may be physical, or emotional, or spiritual and may or may not affect the ones we love.  In addition, the world is always trying to allure us away from our Savior, Jesus Christ, so that we will be ineffective Christians.  If you do not know Christ as personal Savior, overcoming these tests will be more difficult.  For believers, there are three reasons why we must go through what some have called the ‘Refiner’s fire’ – so we may be mature (perfect), entire (Christ like), and pure wanting or in need of nothing.
Temptations and trials make us more mature; the question is not “if” they will come, but “when” will they come?  And when they do come, know that God is working inside of you much needed maturity.  His desire is to use you to help others in similar situations.  Becoming mature will take time; it will also work patience inside of you.  Just as soldiers go through boot camp first or football players go through spring training, so too we will go through a time of training and testing to make us stronger for the upcoming battles of life.  No one is so bad or so far gone that they cannot serve Him.

Consider the people God used in the past:  Abraham was considered old, Jacob lied to get his birthright, Joseph was sold into slavery, Rahab had a seedy past, Moses had a bad temper and killed someone, and David was both a murderer and adulterer.  Yet, God was pleased to use all of them, and He will use you too as long as you willingly go through the trials with Him!

title: Promised Care of God
html:
"﻿6 Therefore humble yourselves under the mighty hand of God, that He may exalt you at the proper time, 7 casting all your anxiety on Him, because He cares for you."  1 Peter 5:6-7﻿
While it is very true that the Lord cares for His own children and for you in particular, we must not forget that the beginning of His promised care begins with this condition: we must humble ourselves “under the mighty hand of God.”

Eating a slice of “humble pie” can be difficult; yet, grace is given to those who are humble (James 4:6). If we want God’s care and providence to operate in our life, we must believe that God helps those who have submitted themselves to Him. Humility is the opposite of pride. Pride tries to convince us we are better than everyone else, we deserve the best in life, and we don’t really need God’s help in our everyday experiences. Pride began in the Garden of Eden (Genesis 3) when Satan convinced Eve that if she partook of the fruit that was not to be eaten, she would not die. All 'pride' questions the plans, motives, and truthfulness of God. Just as Eve disbelieved God’s word, when we live our lives in superiority over others or even over the Lord - how can we expect to even recognize God’s loving kindness in our life?

It is equally as possible that doubt (a seed of pride) can also hinder God’s providence in our life. If we bring up a lot of our worries, sins, and concerns to other people, there is always a possibility they will not believe our concerns are of very much significance. If something is a “big deal” to you, it’s a “big deal” to God; don’t convince yourself that since others don’t care, God must not care either. Coming to such a conclusion will cause lack of trust and lack of faith that God can take care of all your needs. Always remember - God cares for you! But don’t let haughtiness stop you from receiving that care.

title: Proverbs 3:5-6 – Disciples of Jesus are always Trustworthy; trustworthiness is the only hope for America
html:
"5 Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding. 6 In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths."  Proverbs 3:5-6
Being trustworthy and having integrity means that you do the right thing when no one else is looking; when there are times we could be dishonest because we know we could get away with it, we realize that we could not hide our secret sins from the Lord or ourselves.  Such people are given great tasks in the Kingdom of God!
John was trustworthy; as an apostle of the Lord, He loved Jesus and did not abandon Him in the darkest hour.  He was there for Jesus; can Jesus say the same of us?  Are we available every time He calls?  Are we able to adapt to the many changes our church, ministries, or families need us to adapt to?  Do we trust in the Lord with everything we have as well as acknowledging Him (Proverbs 3:5-6)?  He will direct us if we let Him.

While many preachers and teachers are waiting for God to just pour out revival on America, God is waiting for His people to start taking their Christianity seriously and become dependable, available, and trustworthy disciples.  America’s only hope is for dependable disciples of Christ influencing all spheres of society until people see that God is Holy, wonderful, and worthy of all praise.

Return what does not belong to you; fess up when you screw up; don’t steal time or treasures from anyone; don’t take credit for things you haven’t done; and remember to stand up for the helpless among us.  James says it this way:

“Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world.”  James 1:27.  

Believer, you can do it!  Start today.  Learn more, listen to the complete message below.

title: Rejoicing of God’s goodness, even in bad times.
html:
"... the LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD."  Job 1:21b
God has given Christians grace so we can rejoice when life gets tough.  I could spend a long time telling you about, no doubt.  But there are also good times and how you handle the bad times and how you handle the good times is dependent on the type of attitude that you have.  There are some people that are just "hunky dory" and smiling and everything’s going right as long as everything is going right.  But as soon as something bad happens, they get real grumpy and they start blaming everybody.  That’s not the way God wants us to be.  

He wants us to rejoice and again He says rejoice.  But in order for us to rejoice, we have to have his grace.  Having the right attitude and allowing His grace to flow through us will let us get through.  You may not laugh in the middle of turmoil; but there will be an inner peace that allows you to get through the turmoil without biting everybody’s head off. 

God wants us to handle everything with a rejoicing attitude, and we do that through His grace.  We must allow His grace to work in our lives.   The definition for grace is the divine influence upon the heart and its reflection in the life.  In other words, you let God work in your life and then let it flow out so other people can see it.  We become a conduit.  We become a means of transporting God's grace so that everybody can see it in our lives.  If we tell everyone God is good, God can help you, God is merciful, God is gracious, and then something bad happens and we are screaming, yelling and blaming others – those we are trying to witness to might say - What kind of God do you serve?  Do you only serve a happy God? 

No, we serve a mighty God, amen?  And he wants us to be rejoicing no matter what happens good or bad.

title: Romans 14:19 - Be at Peace with Fellow Believers
html:
To truly live in harmony with God, we must learn to live in harmony with others.  

Romans 14:19 encourages Christians to “follow after the things which make for peace, and things wherewith one may edify another.”  All believers can improve on being at peace with one another.  Sometimes we feel that when somebody gets saved that their whole being, life, and experiences must be just like our own because we were saved first!  Perhaps we imagine that if they are to be holy, they must act and think just like “me”.  Problem:  we are all different in our thoughts and actions.  As long as we are following God’s Word and His will together, Let’s be at peace with our differences. 

How do we know if we are at peace with our brethren?  We won’t take the time to tear someone else down; instead, we will try to build them up.  Instead of standing in our smug piety judging the actions of another, we will try to understand them or (as some have put it) try to “walk” in the other person’s shoes before making a judgment.  Are you at peace with fellow believers?  Congratulations!  You are effecting Godly change not only in your local church, but the world over as we build God’s kingdom together.


Are you excited to live in God's grace?  Then keep reading our blog, or listen to the full sermon below.

"Let us therefore follow after the things which make for peace, and things wherewith one may edify another."  Romans 14:19

title: Rut Riders, Backsliders, or Joy Gliders:  How we can learn to thank God, Part 1.
html:
4 They wandered in the wilderness in a solitary way; they found no city to dwell in.
5 Hungry and thirsty, their soul fainted in them.
6 Then they cried unto the LORD in their trouble, and he delivered them out of their distresses.
7 And he led them forth by the right way, that they might go to a city of habitation.

Psalm 107:4-7
After studying Psalm 107, we discover three types of people who are in a relationship with God:  rut riders, back sliders, and joy gliders.  Rut riders are always going in circles; back sliders have a serious relationship problem with God; joy gliders enjoy life so much that if they are not careful, they are not prepared for the storms that may come.  Let’s consider how each type of person can be thankful to God and deepen their friendship with Jesus.

Rut riders can say, “Lord, thank you for finding me!”  Perhaps you can relate to these words:  “They wandered in the wilderness in a solitary way; they found no city to dwell in.” (v.4)  Rut riders are always going in circles, wandering around, repeating the same actions over and over again, and generally feeling lost in this great big wilderness called the world.  The feelings of loneliness and despair become overwhelming; it is like driving around on a rotary and getting so caught up in traffic, you can’t seem to take your exit.  Or maybe you would take the exit, but you’re not sure which exit is the RIGHT one. 

Cry out to God even in the seeming emptiness.  You are not doomed to ride on a circle of the endless daily grind hoping tomorrow will be better.  Tomorrow will be better because God is preparing a place for you that Donald Trump himself would be jealous of!  You don’t have to feel hungry or thirsty anymore (v. 5) because the Lord will deliver you out of the distress and lead you to the way of “habitation” also known as Heaven.  These steps we walk on earth are a preparation for the glory yet awaiting us.

The Lord will fill your soul with His goodness.  Of course, you must be in a relationship with His Son, Jesus Christ.  Do you know the Lord? Click here to learn more.

title: Rut Riders, **Backsliders**, or Joy Gliders:  How we can learn to thank God, Part 2.
html:
4 They wandered in the wilderness in a solitary way; they found no city to dwell in.

5 Hungry and thirsty, their soul fainted in them.

6 Then they cried unto the LORD in their trouble, and he delivered them out of their distresses.

7 And he led them forth by the right way, that they might go to a city of habitation.

8 Oh that men would praise the LORD for his goodness, and for his wonderful works to the children of men!  Psalm 107:4-8
And in other news today, a group of people called backsliders have been identified in God’s word, Psalm 107, as those who were following Him, but then backed away.  These individuals have forgotten what Jesus has done for them, and they have voluntarily put themselves back into the chains of bondage that the Lord had released them from.

The individuals are characterized by those who are no longer bearing the light of God to others because they have gone back into the darkness; they have rebelled against God’s word, the Bible and thus have lost fellowship with Him.  In fact, the Scriptures seem to indicate that they have “despised” the Lord and His teachings.  They knew the grace of God, but deliberately stepped away from His grace.  Normally, this group of people feel great inner turmoil, desiring to follow God again but being tormented by their continual compromises.  Discouragement, despair, and despondency will also be symptomatic of a failure to reestablish fellowship with the Creator of the universe.

If you have identified any of your friends or relatives (or yourself for that matter) as falling under this terrible category of believers, know that the remedy to said situation is to cry unto the Lord (Psalm 107:6).  Such contrite repentance will not go unnoticed by God, and He will deliver backsliders out of their troubles.  Even if the backsliders have turned to addictions like drugs, alcohol, or pleasure – Jesus is able to deliver them and satisfy the hungry soul.  Caution:  going back to the Lord will bring upon the repentant heart such a treasure store of His grace and forgiveness that the one praying will be compelled to praise the Lord for His goodness and show forth all His wonderful works to the children of men!

title: Serving those who cannot serve you.
html:
"So he arose and went to Zarephath. And when he came to the gate of the city, behold, the widow woman was there gathering of sticks: and he called to her, and said, Fetch me, I pray thee, a little water in a vessel, that I may drink."  1 Kings 17:10
1 Kings 17 teaches us that we are tested in many ways to increase our faith.  The prophet of God, Elijah, had no resources for food or water.  While the raven fed him for a little while, the water supply completely dried up.  God said, “9 Arise, get thee to Zarephath, which belongeth to Zidon, and dwell there: behold, I have commanded a widow woman there to sustain thee. 10 So he arose and went to Zarephath.” (v. 9) 

The widow woman to whom God sends Elijah is no better off; she had one son and no means to take care of him.  With no income and a drought occurring in the land, she had run out of resources except for a little flour and two sticks she was going to serve the last bit of food on. How could she be a blessing to anyone?

In our Christian fantasy world, we expect a rich person or someone with good means and resources to rescue us, our ministry, or even our life.  We have become so worldly, we still believe that only rich people can rescue us.  Read the rest of 1 Kings 17 to see how God is able to use two poorest of the poor to exalt His riches!

Here is a challenge to all Pastors, ministries, churches, and congregants:  pray that the Lord would help you serve someone or even a group of people who can’t financially help you in any way, shape, or form.  Walk by faith, expecting that God will meet all your needs as you reach out to others.  God doesn’t want us loving people for what they can give us, but for what we can give them!  This is God’s ways; it is more blessed to give than to receive.  (Acts 20:35)


Want to know more?  Here is the complete audio sermon:

title: Sin and forgiveness taken seriously
html:
If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness. 1 John 1:9
Are we serious in getting rid of things in our life that displease the Lord? If we have understood all the Lord went through when He died for us, we will take sin and the pursuit of forgiveness seriously.

We have not taken sin seriously if we try to obtain forgiveness from someone other than the Lord; sometimes, we feel it's easier to confess our sins to a disinterested party or to someone who we hope will assure us of our right standing before God. Another sign of the lack of seriousness in obtaining forgiveness for wrong doing is is that we try to do good works in the hope of acquiring favor from God. While going to church, volunteering for ministry, or giving money to your local congregation are all commendable actions - they cannot provide the forgiveness necessary to restore lost fellowship with Him.

Instead, let us take seriously God’s plea; He desires fellowship with us and provides a way back to Him. He will never stop loving us, but sin will hinder and stunt our spiritual growth. While society might tell us we must strive for good self esteem, if we are away from God - we must condemn the sin in our life and, through repentance and faith, show the Lord we mean business. This is a voluntary act of our will; we do not merely agree what we have done is wrong but, in a sense, we condemn our sin by abandoning it, turning away from it, ensuring there is no way to fall back into it, and cutting it off completely. Do not fear, however; the Lord is fully able to thrill our hearts so that any sin will soon lose all its attraction as we bask in the glory of the Risen Savior!

title: Start with a Daily Commitment to follow God first
html:
"Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof."  Matthew 6:34
What happened to our spiritual life and the life of our Christian friends?  It seems we were on fire for the Lord, serving Him, and willing to die for Him!  Some who were deeply committed, however, seem to act like they have turned away from the Lord.  Or perhaps you have realized you have walked away from following after Him.  Do you know why this has occurred?

We avoid the Lord and His people because we believe they will judge us for the wrong behaviors we have done or, in the least, we don’t want to have feelings of failure again especially when God’s word challenges us to ever deeper commitments to Him.  Rest assured, a church that has been touched by the grace of God will open up their arms in welcome, no matter where you have been.  Jesus just wants you back today!

Maybe you are not willing to die for Christ, your commitment is not that deep yet.  Are you willing to live for Him?  The Apostle Peter (see the blog post from May 15) was afraid to say that He would die for Jesus a second time; but Jesus accepted His love as a step in the right direction of discipleship. 

Say to the Lord now that you are willing to serve Him today; do not worry about tomorrow, worry about today’s commitment.  Don’t let yesterday trip you up in loving Christ and His kingdom now.  When today is over, then you will make a new commitment for tomorrow; when tomorrow is thru, you will continue taking it step by step, day by day.  If you fall, you will stand back up again and reaffirm your resolve (Proverbs 24:16).  Let nothing stop you as a believer in Christ; three steps forward, two steps back still makes you ahead of the game! 

Consider worshipping with us tomorrow, May 19, 2013 if you do not have a church home.

title: Steadfast in Love for Him by Prayer
html:
"And they continued stedfastly in the apostles' doctrine and fellowship, and in breaking of bread, and in prayers."  Acts 2:42
Some of the greatest works we share together as believers is to pray or share the Lord’s supper with one another.  While there are a very many good things that believers may share together, the activity of interceding on the behalf of others or "breaking of bread" marked the lives of the early church.

When the first Christians broke bread together, they were expressing their love and appreciation for their Lord and Savior who was the ultimate Broken Bread.  They remembered also why it is that they had gathered together as a church: to serve Him, love Him, and worship Him – Christ Jesus, the Messiah!

In addition, they prayed together in worship of God and for each other. 

One of the dying institutes of the church today is the mid-week Prayer session.  You would think that since prayer was the most important part of the early church’s life that we would pray more than once a week.  Sadly, many Christians have settled for a nominal Christian existence, going to churches that appeal more to the flesh in music or “wow” factor messages rather than seeking the face of God.  Prayer is the power of the church; therefore, His power is the only thing that can help us. 

It is thru this type of service, praying together as the church of God, that we can begin forming godly friendship with one another.  As we learn how to pray for each other’s needs, we learn that God has given us gifts to fulfill the work of the body.  As we learn about our gifts, we serve our Savior and the people around us – and as a consequence, we can advance Christ’s kingdom to the end of the world. 

What is stopping us from doing the work of the ministry?  A failure to pray.  What is stopping revival; no seeking hearts.  Why are current last day Christians doomed to a life of the up and down emotional roller coaster ride:  no attempt to pray!

Let’s be about the Father’s business and pray!

Consider visiting us at Berkshire Hills Baptist Church if you find yourself in the Lee, MA area.

title: Steadfast:  Living for Christ Every Single Day
html:
"And the multitude of them that believed were of one heart and of one soul: neither said any of them that ought of the things which he possessed was his own; but they had all things common."  Acts 4:32
Warning; if you love Jesus, but don’t love His church – these blessings can never be yours.  The early church (that is the gathering of Christians in a local area) of Jerusalem experienced great blessings and persecutions, setting the precedent for all future assemblies.  In common they had this - they believed (had faith) and in this, they were of one heart and mind. 
Some rightly point out that we try to isolate ourselves as Christians; instead of fellow shipping with others, we stay by ourselves.  However, power and victory is found living a Christian life along side of other believers in Christ.

We became part of the church of God after, by faith, we accepted Jesus Christ as personal Lord and Savior.  On the Day of Pentecost, 5000 were saved.  Afterward, 3000 more were saved.   Yet, their lives continued to be spiritually enriched all the way through the book of Acts.  They did more than simply believe; they put their faith into action.  Faith in action means we take God literally and believe all His promises are true; we lean on His promises until the faith of Christ is holding us up.

Have you ever watched someone walk a tight rope with a wheel barrel?  Do you believe they are talented enough to do that?  Faith says – we will jump in the wheel barrel and let them roll us to the other side.  So too, in the spiritual life, faith tells us that God will provide for all of our needs, that Christ’s way is better than our way, and that the Bible is the only living book full of all truth.  Do you believe this?  Then start absorbing, obeying, and learning how to walk with Christ by reading the Bible!  Read his Word not just to read black and white text on a page; read it to seek His face ever more diligently.  I can promise you, as you reading in order to search, study, and find God – He will be found and He will put a passion in your heart for Him that no man can extinguish!  Don’t you want to live like this every day?  You can; take a hold of Jesus by faith today!

Listen to the whole sermon here:

title: Taste that the Lord is Good
html:
If so be ye have tasted that the Lord is gracious.  1 Peter 2:3
In some marathons, some runners choose to race carrying a full back pack; while that may not stop someone from finishing the race, it could slow them down from obtaining the goal.  While there is something to be said of endurance training , in the Christian life – we need to be sure we are not running the race with our backpack of sin.  Otherwise, it could slow us down or even stop us all together.

Since the fall of man in Genesis 3, human beings have decided that worldly things are more important than God.  Yet, God says that born again Christians have “tasted that the Lord is gracious.”  In another passage, the Lord invites everyone to “taste and see that the LORD is good:  blessed is the man that trusteth in him” (Psalm 34:8).  If we are allowing our sins and addictions to rule us, we have forgotten how good the Lord is; therefore, He invites us to taste of his precious treasures and see how wonderful it is to know Him.

How do we do this?  We participate in God’s holiness by turning away from sin and replacing our former ways with good works and holiness.  Even though modern day preachers have concocted new or novel formulas, the path to God remains the same.  Some people say following God is too difficult; yet God says that His commandments are not grievous (1 John 5:3) and His burdens are always light (Matthew 11:30.  So why is it so difficult?  Because sin is always grievous and sin’s burdens are always heavy; so, why do we keep running with them in our backpack?  Let’s ask the Lord to remove our weights and besetting sin and follow Him.

title: Titus 2:11-12
html:
While we don’t take a jar full of cookies, place them on the roof, and then tell our two year old they can have some if they can get one – apparently we live our lives as if God has taken His most precious riches, hidden them out of reach,  and then asked us to get them so we can be free!  While our faith is not necessarily effortless, it is neither tortuously difficult (1 John 5:3)
Yet other Christians, thinking living a holy life is impossible, have decided to put no effort whatsoever in their spiritual lives and simply sin all they want.  Believing their soul will go to heaven and their body will not, they have turned God’s grace into a license to sin (even if they choose not to use those words).  This is why Paul warns us, “use not liberty for an occasion to the flesh, but by love serve one another.”  (Galatians 5:13)

In reality, God’s grace is liberating.  It frees us to obey God’s Word, God’s ways, and God’s will.  He would never ask us to do that which He would not equip us to do.  When He says to deny worldly lusts (Titus 2:12), we need not fear His commands.  In fact, we can allow God’s unmerited favor in our life to work through us to love others, serve God, and build His Kingdom!  Are you a kingdom builder?

Please subscribe to our blog and consider listening to the entire sermon below.

"For, brethren, ye have been called unto liberty; only use not liberty for an occasion to the flesh, but by love serve one another."  Galatians 5:17

title: Titus 2:11-12 - Grace Going With Us Everywhere
html:
God’s grace will accompany us through our mental, physical, and spiritual lives.  If we have filled our minds with junk, He can clean it out and fill it with the life giving power of His Word.  If we find ourselves caught up in disobedience, He can help us to live in such a way that we always do the right thing with our only motive being His honor.  And if we are having trouble walking in the path of purity, He can keep us aware that He is walking with us wherever we go.
Scripture says that it is grace that teaches us to live “soberly (right mind), righteously (right actions), and godly (right living).” This means refusing to entertain the worldly clutter that passes as television entertainment, always working hard at our employment even when the boss is not looking, and remembering that Jesus walks daily among us at the coffee shop, church, or motel room or anywhere we go!  Think of the places He would not want you to enter or the actions He would not want you to initiate.  As we learn to separate ourselves from those things that grieve Jesus, He opens the doors to go to places and perform actions that truly fulfill your desire to give Him glory!  You’ll be amazed at how He uses those who fall in love with Him.

Do you know Jesus as Savior and Lord?  Please consider listening to the entire sermon below; if you live in the Berkshires of Massachusetts, consider joining us tomorrow for our Sunday School at 10am and Worship at 11:00am.  Grow in grace!

"Teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly, in this present world;" Titus 2:12

title: Titus 2:11-14 - Grace, God's Gift to All
html:
Grace is God’s undeserved favor working in people’s lives to save and redeem them.  God asks nothing of the person He is helping through grace except faith; He simply asks us to recognize that we are sinners and that we need Christ Jesus as our Savior.  (Ephesians 2:8-9)  No further works like penance, rosary beads, or man made efforts are necessary.  

This does not mean we can use God’s grace as a way to excuse our habits of sin; God wants our bodies to be holy as well.  It is because He expects a holy life from us that His grace restrains us from sin as we submit our lives to His lordship.  In other words, grace frees us from having to participate in sin while we are living here on earth.

Who is eligible in receiving and procuring God’s grace?  Who can begin living in the power of Christ and knowing Him?  “For the grace of God that bringeth salvation hath appeared to all men …”  (Titus 2:11)  All men, women, and children regardless of age or place in life can receive the wonderful gift of grace which results in living in eternal life today.  This grace is free for all mankind!  Won’t you come to Jesus today?

To learn more about a relationship with God, click here.  Consider subscribing to the Grow in Grace Blog.  Or listen to the entire sermon below.

11 For the grace of God that bringeth salvation hath appeared to all men, 12 Teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly, in this present world ... Titus 2:11-12

title: Titus 2:12 - Teaching Grace
html:
Everyday, grace can teach Christians how to act, what to believe, and how to serve.  Required on our part is being teachable every day and always listening to God’s word so we can become more like Christ. 
To be taught by God’s grace (Titus 2:11-12) means to be trained like children, and to be corrected where necessary.  Once we have learned to go on the correct path of holy living, it is our responsibility to be our brother’s keeper.  Don’t just complain that others are not as righteous as we are; reach out in a non judgmental way and give a helping hand by simply saying, “That’s not what God expects of us.”  Sometimes, a short exhortation is all that is needed.

But what are the lessons of Grace?  The first one is to deny “ungodliness” which means to refuse to live contrary to God just like the world does.  When we lack holy reverence for God’s Word by not listening or obeying them or when we refuse to accept the path that He has given us in life – we live “ungodly”.  Don’t ignore God’s will; embrace it as your own.  As we study and learn God’s grace together, expect to grow more and more like Christ.

What other lessons does God’s grace have for us? Subscribe to our blog or listen to the entire sermon below.  Do you live in the Lee, Massachusetts area?  Please consider joining us for our Sunday morning services; click this link here.

"11 For the grace of God that bringeth salvation hath appeared to all men,12 Teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly, in this present world;"  Titus 2:11-12

title: What Happens When We Fail? Part 1
html:
17 He saith unto him the third time, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me? Peter was grieved because he said unto him the third time, Lovest thou me? And he said unto him, Lord, thou knowest all things; thou knowest that I love thee. Jesus saith unto him, Feed my sheep. John 21:17
This week’s blogosphere will focus on answering a common question in the Christian life; what happens if we fail the Lord?  In today’s Bible reading, the Lord had asked Simon Peter questions about the fervency of his love for Him; this came about as a result of Peter’s sin of denying the Lord.  Even though Peter had made promises to Jesus not to forsake Him and even die for Him (Mark 14:31), when the Roman guards captured Jesus – Peter abandoned Jesus and told a group of inquiring women that he did not even know who Jesus was. (John 18)

All of us, from time to time, will fail to do what is right for the Lord.  Often times, we fail in our commitments and promises to follow God.  Someone makes a promise, they break the promise, the fail to follow the Lord, they feel guilty because of the failure, so they decide to forsake the Lord all together!  All broken promises to God lead to separation from the Lord.  Why?

Sometimes we interpret failures as a “stop sign”.  (Isn’t it funny some of us run right through real stop signs on the road, but we stop in our spiritual life at failures!)  Instead, interpret failures as a “caution” sign; the failures help us to step back, look a little closer at what we have promised the Lord to do, and go forward with more knowledge of the limitations we have:  all while still serving Him!

How can we turn failures in successes in our walk with Him?  Can’t wait for the rest of the series?  Listen to the sermon below.

title: What Happens When We Fail?  Part 2
html:
"15 So when they had dined, Jesus saith to Simon Peter, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me more than these? He saith unto him, Yea, Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Feed my lambs. 16 He saith to him again the second time, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me? He saith unto him, Yea, Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Feed my sheep. 
17 He saith unto him the third time, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me? Peter was grieved because he said unto him the third time, Lovest thou me? And he said unto him, Lord, thou knowest all things; thou knowest that I love thee. Jesus saith unto him, Feed my sheep." John 21:15-17
What happens when we fail the Lord?  Simple answer:  he starts off where we have failed and shows us mercy.

Peter had previously denied knowing Jesus and back pedaled on his promise to die for Him.  When Jesus asked him, Peter do you love me – in the Greek, He asked Peter twice, “Peter, do you love me enough to die for me?”  But instead of recommitting himself to loving Jesus to die for him, both times Peter responded, “yes, you know I love you like a brother.”  Finally, Jesus asked, “Do you love me like a brother” to which Peter “grieved” and reaffirmed his brotherly affection for Christ.  Perhaps Peter was sorrowful, having remembered his previous failures.  Perhaps, Peter was hesitant to make promises to the Lord again having learned from his failures the first time.  Or maybe he was simply remorseful to relive his mistake in his mind over and over again.  No matter what, Jesus was not done with Peter and He is never done with us!  Hallelujah!

Perhaps we made promises to the Lord to be close to Him, to read our Bibles faithfully every day under a certain schedule, or to accomplish a certain task for Him.  Then, when we do read the Bible or listen to a sermon, our hearts are pierced at our inability to perform said task.  Don’t despair; the Lord is willing and waiting to hear from you and start with you right where you are.  Sometimes we try to take humungous steps when we’re not ready; rest assured, He will always be waiting for us and ready to forgive and pardon.  Get back to fellowship with God today.

title: What If I Am Not Perfectly Holy?
html:
"Follow peace with all men, and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord" Hebrews 12:14
We are to follow after God’s holiness; as believers in Christ, we are to be holy because He is holy (1 Peter 1:16).  Since we are to imitate God in all His ways, let’s live in His holiness.  This does not mean we look down on the spirituality of other people; instead, it means we think others better than ourselves in all our ways while striving to obey Him.  We ought not live holy because it is our duty; instead, we ought to live holy because of what He has done for us.  C.T. Studd says, “If Jesus Christ be God and died for me, then no sacrifice can be too great for me to make for Him.”

But under such high expectations, what if we fail?  Even though we know that God loves us immensely, will He throw us away or cause us to cease from serving Him?

In the Old Testament, sometimes the holy vessels of the temple would become unclean.  Did God immediately throw all of them away?  No, through a process of cleansing – the vessels would become holy again and returned into the service of God.

So too, your momentary falters or occasional weaknesses or, in some instances, constant failings will not cause God to stop using you.  Even if He changes your service options, if you would submit yourself into His care – He will cleanse your heart and conscience and return you to His service.  Do not fear; though you are not perfect, the Perfect One will lay a foundation of holiness in your life one day at a time!

title: 02.04.19 - The Sabbath Restores Our Soul
html:
8 Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy. Exodus 20:8

     We do not keep the Sabbath in order to go to heaven; we keep the Sabbath day holy because we are citizens of Heaven and we have entered into God’s rest. Be warned, do not rely on worshiping either on the Sabbath Day (Saturday) or on the Lord’s Day (Sunday) to be enough to enter God’s Kingdom. Only faith in Christ and His work on the cross can bring us to glory.
     Yet, we believe in the principle of resting one day in the week as obedience to God’s commands. It is not another check mark on a list of things to do; rather, it is a joy to look forward to gathering once a week with other believers. In fact, it restores our soul.
Psalm 23 reminds us that the Lord restores our soul. Remembering to take one day off in the week to worship God is His way to restore us. The idea of rest (Sabbath) is mentioned 89 times in the Old Testament and 62 times in the New Testament. Even Jesus took time to rest His soul while on the earth. (Mark 4:35-40)
     While there are some jobs that may require people to work seven days a week and even longer, our bodies were not meant to continue working perpetually. If you find yourself skipping this once a day rest, think about praying and asking the Lord to help you take Sunday off to worship Him; you can rest in all the victories and even recover from the defeats of the previous week and look toward the next six days as another adventure from Him.
 
To learn more about the 4th commandment, listen to last Sunday’s message on the Sabbath!

title: 02.06.2019 - The Sabbath reminds us God wants us to work
html:
8 Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy. 9 Six days shalt thou labour, and do all thy work … Exodus 20:8-9
 
     Today, we have chosen to worship God on Sunday because it is the first day of the week, the same day the Lord Jesus was resurrected. We remember the Lord who has given us all blessings. It’s not only to rest our bodies, but also to help us remember who gave us this body so we can work.
     It’s completely true, the Sabbath rest infers that God wants us to work! Some take this to the extreme (Christians and non-Christians alike) and work 81 hours, 7 days a week, to accumulate as much money as they can in this life. They forgot the Lord’s blessings that have allowed them to be able to work and have the strength to make their money. It is doubtful anyone would ever read on someone’s tombstone “I wish I could work one more day.”
     Still, others swing the pendulum in the opposite direction and work not at all; this is not referring to those who are now retired, but rather those who are simply lazy. We are expected to work; Paul has told us that “if any would not work, neither should he eat” (2 Thessalonians 2:10). Just as God gave Adam and Eve a job to do in the Garden of Eden, so He has given us tasks not for ourselves, but to help others.
     There are legitimately other people who have needs they cannot meet for themselves; we have been called to work six days so we may “give to him that needeth” (Ephesians 4:28). Then, our rest is truly glorious and restorative because we thank Him for the blessing He has made us for other people who need it.
 
If you haven’t had a chance, listen to this week’s sermon on the Sabbath!

title: 02.08.19 - The Sabbath Day helps us remember Christ
html:
11 For in six days the LORD made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that in them is, and rested the seventh day: wherefore the LORD blessed the sabbath day, and hallowed it.
 
     It’s fascinating that the more conveniences that we have in our modern world, the busier we have become. Washing machines, automobiles, and the Internet have not made us less busy … instead, busier! But, the Sabbath Day is a holy day, a consecrated day, and a day for our personal sanctification. Let us take Sunday as a day to remember what God has done for us; don’t worry about tomorrow because tomorrow “shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof.” (Matthew 6:34)
     And what did Jesus do? What can we remember on Sunday as we set the day apart for worship? Some call it the Christian Sabbath; some the Lord’s day. It is on the first day of the week that the early followers of Jesus went to the tomb and realized that Jesus had been resurrected from the dead! The payment for our sins had been completed, and He was raised victoriously. Acts 20:7, 1 Corinthians 16:2, and all the gospels attest to how special the ‘1st day of the week’ became for the early churches.
     We encourage you this week and especially this coming Lord’s Day, think of the Sabbath as a day of rest, as a day of God showing how much He loves you and cares for you, and as a time to rest from all the work that the Lord has given you to do with your hands.

title: 05.19.2020 - Our righteousness no good for Heaven!
html:
If we try to be good on our own or even if we try to mix our good works with God’s good works, we’ll never make it to heaven! But, if you're going to heaven, you need to have perfect righteousness. But, this righteousness cannot be your own because there is “none righteous, no not one (Romans 3:10)”.

Your attempts to live a holy life to earn salvation comes from your self effort or from following the law or from being a nice person. Unfortunately, there are so many people in this world who say, "I'm going to heaven because I've lived a good life." They're relying on their own righteousness. In fact, they could follow every one of the ten commandments, and that still wouldn't be good enough!
 
So, how, then, can we get into heaven? We are told in Philippians 3:9 that we're “found in him, not having mine own righteousness, which is of the law, but that which is through the faith of Christ, the righteousness which is of God by faith." So when we have faith in God, when we have faith that brings salvation, then we have righteousness.
 
God's righteousness (a righteousness outside of ourselves) is what we need. When we trust Jesus Christ as our Savior by faith, we can have our sins forgiven, and then we are given the righteousness of Christ which belongs to God! Believe on Jesus Christ and put your trust completely on what He did on the cross (He died, shed His blood, was buried, and rose the third day). When the day of judgement comes, God will not look at our righteousness, but on Christ, His Son, who obeyed the law perfectly.
 
Pray something like this. “Dear Jesus, by faith I believe that only Jesus can save me from my sins because He is perfect and holy. Thank you for dying on the cross for my sins; I repent of my sins and believe completely on Jesus for eternal life. Thank you Lord for giving me a new life in Christ! Amen.”

title: 08.21.2023 - As a Believer, You are a Soldier in War
html:
3 Thou therefore endure hardness, as a good soldier of Jesus Christ.
4 No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life; that he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier. 2 Timothy 2:3-4
 
In case, you didn't know this, we are in spiritual war. All believers have been entrusted by Jesus Christ to be spiritual warriors. You enlisted when you turned your back on the old life of sin and turned toward Christ for eternal life. Some people, however, have not fulfilled their purpose. Just like in a real army, you may be assigned to different places and you’re expected to fulfill an important role within that command; Jesus Christ is our loving but firm commanding officer and we seek to do what he asks of us to be a good soldier and a good witness to those around us.

Ephesians 6:11-12 informs us that we must put on the spiritual armor of God to withstand spiritual battles; the more our faith grows, the more Satan will try to tear us down and try to convince us to defect.

One way he does this is by trying to get us to be entangled in the affairs of this life. That's the thing that gets to us sometimes. We get so caught up in daily living that we lose track of why God has left us in this world. In Luke chapter 8, when Jesus talked about the parable of the sower, one of the seeds fell among thorns. They are described as “they which when they had heard go forth and are choked with the cares and riches and pleasure of this world and bring no fruit to perfection."

This week, let’s challenge ourselves not to get entangled with the cares, pleasures, or riches of this world. This week, let’s challenge ourselves to go back to weekly church attendance (unless we are unable to take care of our family without working on Sunday) and get back to daily devotions. These core basics help train us for the battle ahead.

title: 08.23.2023 - Run to Win an Eternal Prize
html:
5 And if a man also strive for masteries, yet is he not crowned, except he strive lawfully.
2 Timothy 2:5

24 Know ye not that they which run in a race run all, but one receiveth the prize? So run, that ye may obtain. 25 And every man that striveth for the mastery is temperate in all things. Now they do it to obtain a corruptible crown; but we an incorruptible.
1 Corinthians 9:24-25

Paul liked sporting events. He referred a lot to running a race or enduring a marathon. You can learn from athletes who strive for “masteries”; if you want to run a successful race as a believer, you must run according to God’s rules and ways. The prize is a good conscience for having done your best, and future rewards for service - all for the love of the Savior!
 
First, you must understand your goal. From 1st Corinthians 9:24, Paul says “run that ye may obtain” an incorruptible crown. This means that the shiny things we strive for in this life are nothing in comparison to the rewards God has for us. There's a prize at the end of the race. Know what that prize is. What are you running through life to obtain? Fame? Glory? Money? Worldly comfort? That's a corruptible crown. Or are you running for an Incorruptible Crown, that crown of rejoicing, that crown of righteousness?
 
Second, know what you are racing for. Just like an athlete, what do they race for? They race for that crown or reward at the end of the race tack. They practice, knowing that's their end destination - the finish line!
 
How many people enter a race so they can place second? Third? Do people think third out of 14 is good enough?  No, we enter the race because we want to win. And that's what Paul says. When you enter the Christian race, you realize there's a goal line and your goal is to finish the race strongly. "He said I've run the course, I finished my race. There's laid up for me a crown of righteousness." (2 Tim 4:6-8)
 
What about you? Are you running to get earthly rewards in this life? The world will have you think their plans are the most important goal in the world. But don’t listen to them; there is only one race that matters: running a race that is well pleasing to God, showing true Christ-like love toward our neighbor, and increasing in godliness and holiness. Run to win!
