Outline

I. Mercies Motivate — We give ourselves to God because of His mercy.

II. Bodies Offered — We present ourselves as living sacrifices.

III. World Resisted — We refuse to be conformed to the world.

IV. Minds Renewed — We are transformed by changing how we think.

V. Will Revealed — We learn and live out God’s good, acceptable, and perfect will.


(Transcribed by TurboScribe. Go Unlimited to remove this message.)

Romans chapter 12. Now as we've been studying through the book of Romans, the first 11 chapters, to be honest, they're kind of tough to handle. There's a lot of things that are spoken of that we really have to delve deep in to understand, but that's because it's mostly doctrine.

It's mostly telling us, it's 11 chapters are basically saying this. The Jews had their chance and they messed up, so the Gentiles got a chance now, but the truth is, all have sinned and come short of the glory of God. In fact, last week we looked at verse 32 of chapter 11.

For God hath concluded them all in unbelief that he might have mercy upon all. Now starting in chapter 12 for the rest of the book, it's more of a instruction manual, how to live when you've accepted that mercy of God, how to be a disciple of Jesus Christ. Now being a disciple is different than just being a believer.

You can be a believer without being a disciple, but you can't be a disciple without being a believer. There's a lot of people that say, yeah, I believe in God, but the way they live, somebody once termed it was Christian atheism. Christian atheism is you say you believe there's a God, but you live like there isn't.

But God wants us to be disciples. And here in this first two verses, it starts off informing us some of the things that we need to put into our life and understand so we can be good disciples, good followers, good learners of God. Let's read the first two verses of chapter 12, and then we'll dissect them a little bit.

I beseech you, therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that you present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service. And be not conformed to this world, but be you transformed by the renewing of your mind that you may prove what is that good and acceptable and perfect will of God. These are great verses.

I think sometimes we ought to read these on a regular basis to remind us. Notice he starts off, I beseech you, therefore, brethren. That's Paul saying, I urge you, I exhort you.

What I'm going to tell you is important. Notice it's not a command, but it's an exhortation. It's not something that he says, you have to do this or you'll lose your salvation. 

It's something that you have to do this because of your salvation. And he calls them brethren. So we know these verses are not written to anybody except for those who are brothers and sisters in Christ. 

Brethren. He also writes it by the mercies of God. That word by really means through or because of. 

The things that we do to become disciples are because of the mercies of God. As we just read before, that God considered everybody in unbelief so he could show his mercy on us. That word mercy. 

Great, great word. Just means to have compassion. God had compassion on us. 

Because we could have all died and gone to hell. But because of Jesus Christ, he showed his compassion. Because of Jesus Christ, he showed his grace.

And through our faith, we've trusted him. And we know we have eternal life. But unfortunately, friends, we have to live today. 

And if you read the papers or watch the news or just gained your information somewhere else, this is a sinful world we're living in. Somebody said once, if God doesn't do something soon, he has to apologize to Sodom and Gomorrah. It's that bad. 

But the thing is, is what the world will try to tell you is you need to go along to get along. If you try to tell anybody what you do is against the word of God, you're being judgmental. I find it fascinating. 

You tell somebody, a friend or a family member, somebody else something that they're doing you know is extremely sinful, you say, God says that's sinful. They'll tell you that you're a hater, that you don't love people. You're being judgmental. 

Well, just by them telling you you're a hater, they're being judgmental towards you. Seems kind of ironic, doesn't it? But instead, God wants us to live a life that shines. Live a life that's different. 

That's why he says, because of the mercies of God, first of all, you present your bodies a living sacrifice. That's the first step in being a disciple, presenting your bodies a living sacrifice. Just think about sacrifices, especially the Jewish sacrifices. 

They brought an animal, tell them you're not home. You bring an animal and you offer it up. But here's the thing, once you give that animal to be offered as a sacrifice, you no longer have control over that sacrifice. 

And that sacrifice has no control over itself. But the thing is, it's a once and done sacrifice, a dead sacrifice. Once it's offered, that's it. 

But what God wants from you, he wants you to be a living sacrifice. He wants you to give yourself to him voluntarily, by choice, to be used by him for his purpose. A living sacrifice.

That's why I believe in Jesus. We read in Matthew some verses, it's also in Luke, in Luke 9, 23, he said to them all, if any man will come after me, let him deny himself, take up his cross daily and follow me. That's what a living sacrifice is. 

It's a choice you have to make. I'm going to give my whole self to God today. And then tomorrow, you got to do it again.

Every day, we offer a living sacrifice to God. A sacrifice that is daily occurrence. The sacrifice where we give ourselves to him. 

In Romans 6, 13, it says, neither yield ye your members as instruments of unrighteousness unto sin, but yield yourselves unto God as those that are alive from the dead and your members as instruments of righteousness unto God. When we give ourselves over to be a living sacrifice, we're giving ourselves over to live like Christ. To walk around clothed in his righteousness. 

And that's kind of hard. I understand. Depending on where you work and the people you're around, you start trying to live Christ-like, the first thing they do is going to make fun of you.

They made fun of Jesus. The first thing they're going to do is any supposed thing that you do that doesn't match their idea of Christianity, they're going to say, well, if you were a good Christian, then you would do this. That's okay. 

They told Jesus the same thing. He ate with sinners and publicans. And they said, see, you're just like them. 

No, he didn't eat with them to be like them. He ate with them to show that they could be like him. So it also tells us in first Peter 2, 5, you as lively stones are build up a spiritual house, a holy priesthood to offer up spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God by Christ Jesus. 

We are to be a living sacrifice, a daily choice you make, a choice that will change your life. Maybe not at first, but you'll start to feel more joy. You'll start to feel more contentment.

The more you walk with Jesus, the more you give yourself as a living sacrifice. But it also tells us you present your body as a living sacrifice, holy. That's H-O-L-Y, not W-H-O-L.

It's also W-H-O-L-Y, a living sacrifice, all of you, but it's also a holy sacrifice. And this holiness really has three different ideas. You know, when God tells us to be holy, one of the things he wants us to do is to be pure.

To be holy means to be pure, to be physically pure, to keep from sin, to keep from lust, to keep from doing any of those things. The world will tell you something different. God says be holy. 

Be holy for what? For I am holy. Now, I always say this. I'm going to repeat it.

When it says be holy, it doesn't mean be holier than now. It means be holy, be pure. Just like Jesus was pure, outwardly sinless.

But it also means to be morally pure. That's the inward part, to know that you are set apart, to know that you are pure within. There's a lot of people pretend to be Christians, but if you could read their mind, you'd go, what are you thinking? He wants us to be pure, not on the outside only, but also on the inside, to be set apart, to be pure as he is pure. 

And how do we do that? We do it through the word of God. And we do it by allowing the Holy Spirit that dwells within us to guide us, direct us. I don't know about you, but if you're on the internet, if you're on TV or anything, suddenly these images pop up that your mind wants to drift to something impure. 

Don't let it. If you do temporarily sin through the lust of the flesh and the lust of the mind, just instantly say, Lord, forgive me. A good idea would be, Lord, forgive me and take those images out of my mind.

That's being morally pure, knowing instantly that you've sinned, knowing instantly you need to request forgiveness for that sin. That can be hard. But the thing is, it's possible.

Because you made yourself a living sacrifice, now you need to be holy. But it also means to be what I call ceremonially holy. In other words, set apart for God's use. 

That's what holiness also means, to be set apart for God's use. Remember, have you ever studied the old tabernacle? You walk in, you got the table to show bread, and you got the light stand over here, and you got the altar of incense. Those things, they were inanimate, but they were called holy objects to God. 

Why was that? Because they were used specifically by God for his purpose. But what happened if somebody, in moving the, say, table to show bread, dropped it and got it all dirty? Oh no, it's no longer holy because now it's all messed up. You know what they did? They cleaned it up, and they rededicated it to God, and now it once again become holy. 

Now knowing that, 1 John 1.9 gives us a verse that says, if you confess your sins, he's faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to what? Cleanse us from all unrighteousness. It literally means if you sin, you confess it, he'll forgive you and return you back to that holy function he has planned for you. A believer can always be used by God. 

Sometimes believers will sin. Sometimes they will do things that in their mind, especially Satan, will come upon them and say, God doesn't love you. God can't use you anymore. 

You're done. That's a lie, a lie directly from Satan. Now, just to clarify, there are some sins that you can do that will disqualify you from some of the things God may have wanted you to do, but he will always use you in some other place.

Does that make sense? All right. Plan B. God's got a plan B. You say, well, what do you mean? Well, let's say, oh, heaven forbid, you have somebody in church that likes to work with the children, likes to work in BBS and stuff, but for some reason, whether it's his fault or not, her fault or not, they get accused of child molestation or child whatever. You don't want them working with your kids anymore, because not only is that a bad thing for God, it's a bad thing for the church, but God will have something else for them to do once they sought forgiveness and got help and things like that. 

God can use them someplace else, but not in the same place. God wants to use you. Why? Because you should be holy, set apart. 

Now, what's the next one? A living sacrifice, holy, acceptable to God. That means as you're doing your holiness, it should be something that's acceptable to God. There's a lot of people, and you probably know some of them, that say they're good church goers or they're good Christians or they're good holy people, but man, you listen to them talk, gossip, gossip, gossip, judgmental, judgmental, judgmental.

That's not acceptable to God. That's not a way to be holy. We need to do what is acceptable to God.

How do we know what's acceptable to God? Through the guidance of the Holy Spirit and His word. Amen? If someone tries to tell you something that's not here, that doesn't match with this, don't do it. Because God's given us 66 books, and to me, that's enough to try to follow.

Why would I want something else? So we need to be acceptable unto God, to be an acceptable sacrifice, to be what God wants you to be and not what you want to be. And that's a big thing. You know, we see the advertisement, be what you want to be. 

No, you need to be what God wants you to be. If God wants you to be a multimillionaire, God knows you can handle being a multimillionaire. But if God knows that if you start becoming a multimillionaire, that you'll never fellowship with other believers anymore and you'll start falling into other vices and sins, God doesn't want you there. 

Where you are is where God wants you. When you give yourself over as a living sacrifice. Because once you, just like a dead sacrifice, once the sacrifice is offered, and in the Old Testament, the high priest took it, once the high priest had it, the person who offered it had no control over what was going to happen. 

Only the priest and God did. And when you give your bodies as a living sacrifice to God, you give up total control of what you need to do and want to do. You give it to God. 

You let God decide what you're going to do. You let God decide where you're going to go. You say, well, how do I do that? How about a little prayer? How about listening to the Holy Spirit? Many times, people end up doing what they want to do, Christians, and then they become dissatisfied. 

They become bitter or angry. And it says that when you give your bodies a living sacrifice, when you are holy, acceptable to God, that is your reasonable service. Service means worship or service. 

It's reasonable. It's just logical. You're saying, well, wait a minute. 

It sounds pretty unreasonable to me. Me, give total control to God? Yeah. God says that's just reasonable.

That's just what you should be doing. Don't fight it. Do it. 

Now, the next verse helps us to understand all of these things. Verse two, and be not conformed to this world. Conformed means to be fashioned or to have the same pattern.

Don't, as a Christian, don't try to match your life to what the world thinks you should be. Don't be conformed to the world. First John, chapter two, verse 15. 

Love not the world, neither the things that are in the world. If any man loved the world, the love of the Father is not in him. For all that's in the world, the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life is not of the Father, but of the world. 

And the world passeth away, and the lust thereof, but he that doeth the will of God abideth forever. The world's always trying to make Christians more like them. In fact, sadly, there's a lot of Christian churches that have decided to have worldly standards in order to attract more people.

God don't like that, I don't think. You get a lot of people, but on the other hand, what do you attract them to? Worldly things. And if you start convincing people that, yeah, this is a worldly thing, but we're doing it for God, then that gives them permission to do whatever they want to and say, well, it must be from God. 

But God has standards. Don't be conformed to this world. The world says, well, it's okay if you dress the way you want to dress.

And by that, I mean, it's getting to be summertime, folks. Both men and women walking around half naked is not, I believe, the way God wanted us to be. I mean, Adam and Eve tried that just a little bit. 

They had just a few fig leaves. God says, that's not good enough. I'm going to sew you a bigger garment out of a sheepskin.

Just something to think about. The world says, it's okay to go wherever you want to as long as you still worship God. It's just like in the old world when Christianity first started.

They say, if you want to work here, you have to worship this God. If you want to be in this, what do you call it, guilds, I think Peter said, or like unions. If you want to be in that, you had to worship a certain God. 

Some good Christians lost a lot of jobs because they were not worshiping any other God but Jehovah. But the world says, well, it's just a job. You don't have to mean what you say. 

Wait, if you don't mean what you're saying, that's called lying, right? It's called being a hypocrite. And God doesn't want us to be hypocrites in order to satisfy the world just so we can get along and not have any problems. But sometimes we do. 

We've got to be very careful about that. So be not conformed to the world. If you're giving yourself a living sacrifice, it's not like the world. 

If you're trying to live like the world and talk like the world, it's just not the way to be. Ephesians chapter four, it says that you put off concerning the former conversation, the old man, which is corrupt according to the deceitful lust and be renewed in the spirit of your mind that you put on the new man, which after God is created in righteousness. That's why it says we're to be transformed by the renewing of your mind.

Transformed means to change. Literally, it's the word, the word we have for metamorphosis is the word they use here to be transformed. How do we do it? By the renewing of your mind.

Here's a great truth. If you're a believer and the Holy Spirit dwells within you, you cannot be possessed by the devil. Unbelievers can, but a believer can't because the Holy Spirit's within you and the devil tries to possess you. 

The Holy Spirit says, uh-uh. The way the devil messes with you is with your mind, by the things you see and you start thinking and it'll start you thinking different. But this says in order to be a living sacrifice, in order to be holy, you need to renew your mind. 

Start thinking differently. That's your whole thing. That's your intellect, your will, your emotions, everything. 

Start thinking differently. Start thinking like God, amen? Think like God does so you can change, transform by the renewing of your mind. And when you start thinking differently and start thinking like God, then we'll start putting things away that we used to think were okay. 

Let's see if any of these hit home with you. Ephesians 4, 25 to 29. Wherefore, put away lying. 

Speak every man truth with his neighbor. If we are members, one of another. Be ye angry, but sin not. 

Let not the sun go down upon your wrath. Neither give place to the devil. Let him that steal, steal no more. 

But rather let him labor, working with his hands a thing which is good, that he may have to give to him that need it. Let no corrupt communication proceed out of your mouth, but that which is good to edify. That means building up. 

That it may minister grace to the hearers. See, that's where we start to change. Things that the world used to say was okay, God says it's not okay. 

You can change. You've got to start with thinking. I know we'll all be tempted sometimes.

That part about lying. Oh, yeah, yeah. You're with a coworker, and they may ask you some question. 

There's always a loaded question. And you'll be tempted to lie. Or with a husband, or with a wife, or with a family member. 

They'll ask you a question. And you want to be kind. You want to be honest. 

But you don't want to hurt their feelings. That's when you really need the Holy Spirit working in you to give you the right answer. You know what I mean? And he will. 

A little quick prayer. Lord, give me the right answer, but also allow them to accept it graciously. That always helps. 

And I like the part about let him that steal, steal no more. But let him work so that those who do have needs, not those that won't work, those who do have needs, you can help not only yourself and your family, but help those that have needs. But the government's already taken that over, and it messed it all up. 

They decided to give it to whoever wanted it. But really, Scripture says, no, if you can work, you should what? Work. And then you can help other people.

So be transformed by the renewing of your mind. So why do we not want to be conformed to the world, doing what the world does? No matter what it is, if God says no, the answer is no. Instead, change our mind, our thinking. 

Why should we do that? For the very last part, that you may prove, that means test, what is that good and acceptable and perfect will of God? You want to know, everybody, every believer always says, you know, when you start talking about the will of God, they'll go, I don't know what the will of God is in my life. Well, if you give your life over as a sacrifice, if you become holy, if you don't become conformed to the world, and you start transforming your mind, then you'll know what the will of God is for your life. It doesn't just happen. 

There's things that you have to do first. Many times when you find out what the will of God is for your life, you're going to go, wow, wow. I know a lot of missionaries, and a lot of missionaries that have gone to the field, when they were growing up in high school and stuff, you said you're going to be a missionary to Timbuktu. 

They go, no, I'm not. I'm going to be wealthy. God changed it. 

But there's a lot of people that thought, I'm always going to be a missionary, but God changed it and put them someplace else. See, when you give your life over to God and over to his control, when you're determined to be holy and change your mind and the way you think, to think like God, God will definitely show you what the will is, that good will. That means that which benefits somebody, either yourself or somebody else. 

Perfect will, complete. What was the third one? Acceptable, what God wants. It's not what you want. 

It's what God wants. And many times when we see what God's will is for our life, we ask ourselves, oh, Lord, is this really? You've got to be kidding me. But God wants to use each and every one of us that's a believer. 

Do you believe that? Say amen. Will he use you the way you want to? Eh, sometimes. But the bottom line is it takes a choice on your part to get to where God will show you what he wants from you. 

You need to become a living sacrifice, give God control. Part of that is being holy, both in your mind and in your actions. To not be conformed to the world, but be transformed, changed by the renewing of your mind. 

Start thinking like God does. Doesn't Scripture say we have the mind of Christ? We need to put that in action in our lives. What the world needs to see is believers who are living what the book teaches. 

Not what we hope it says, what it really says. Let's be those believers. Let's be that part of God's family that says, from this point on, God, you have control of my life. 

Let the Holy Spirit work within me. If I sin, Lord, forgive me. If I've been conformed to the world in any way, Lord, show me what that is.

Whether it's the lust of the flesh, or the lust of the eyes, or the pride of life. And by the way, if you're wondering some examples on that, read the instance where Jesus went to the wilderness and a devil tried to work on him. Because those three things, the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, are the same three types of sin that the devil tried to tempt Jesus with.

That's your homework assignment. Let's bow our heads. As a believer, first of all, I hope you are a believer. 

I hope you have trusted Jesus Christ by faith. You believe that He died to your sins, that He rose the third day. You believe that He did it for you. 

And if you believe that, do you consider yourself a disciple, a follower, a learner of Jesus Christ? Not just a believer, but actively working on becoming a disciple, a true learner. When you follow God's will, He'll allow you to know it's your will. You'll work together, but then you'll find joy, you'll find peace, you'll find fullness of life.

Before we pray, think about what Peter said in 1 Peter 4-2, talking about a believer, that he no longer shall live the rest of his time in the flesh to the lust of men, but to the will of God. We decide we take these verses and put it in our lives so we will know and follow the will of God. Let's all pray. 

Heavenly Father, Lord, just two simple verses with so many truths. Help each one of us here, Lord, first of all, to be assured that they know Jesus Christ as their Savior. And then, Lord, to be determined that we will be disciples. 

We will give our life over as a living sacrifice each and every day. We will, Lord, not be conformed to the world, but we'll allow our minds to be transformed so that we can live the way you want us to live, that we can share your word with other people and show them that the love of God expands to everybody. Help us, Lord, to be the kind of believers, the kind of disciples that you desire us to be, Lord. 

Use us in service. Thank you, Lord. In Jesus' name, amen.

title: 06.23.2024 - All for the Glory of God
html:
Our actions and the things that we say have an effect on the lives of others. Worshiping and praising God begins at church. But, we must continue glorifying the Lord in our relationships with each other. Our deeds and words might bring someone closer to the Lord ... or drive them away. Which do you want to do? 
Download File Link MP3
​06.23.2024 - All for the Glory of God
by Pastor Dr. Doug Mann
Berkshire Hills Baptist Church, Lee, MA

As we've been looking in 1 Corinthians, the last couple chapters we've noticed that there was a problem in the church of Corinth. Corinth had a lot of temples to false gods, they had idol worship, and the people would take meat, offer it to the idol, and then sell it to be eaten, and part of their sacrifice was eating the meat offered to the idols. And then people started getting saved, they started accepting Christ as their Savior by faith, and the problem arose, what are we going to do about meat now? Because all the meat has been offered to an idol.
 
And numerous times in 1 Corinthians, Paul discusses this, so it must have been a big problem. But we can apply it to our life today, and as we look at this section here, verses 23 to 33, we're going to notice something. I don't know about you, but almost everyone I know has a goal for their life, or some guidelines they want to live by, or a basis that they want to live by.
 
I think it pretty much covers everybody. Some people just, their goal is to be rich. Some people want to be popular.
 
Some people want to be powerful. That's all the politicians, for all of those. Sometimes our goal is just to survive from day to day.
 
Yet, for a Christian, this section tells us what your overreaching, your number one goal should be, to give glory to God. And so whatever we do, as we're going to see in Scripture, it means giving God the glory. So as Paul starts off in this section, we have to understand that when Paul starts talking about doing things, not doing things, he's not talking about sinful things or immoral things.
 
He's more talking about things that may not be wrong per se, yet for some people they may be considered wrong. And those are the people we have to take into account. You know the old saying, no man's an island, is not true in Christianity.
 
We must all look out for each other. I believe that's the purpose of what Jesus said. If you're my followers, you will what? Have love, one for another.
 
We need to care for one another. And this applies both to caring for those that are believers and even those that are unbelievers, as we're going to see. So for all things not immoral, we do have freedom.
 
In verse 23, Paul says, all things are lawful for me, but all things are not expedient. All things are lawful for me. All things edify not.
 
Let no man seek his own, but every man another's wealth. Verse 23 and 24. Here, notice that we have freedom as believers to do things we may not have done as unbelievers.
 
We have freedom to know that when I leave this life, I'm going to be in heaven. Now we don't have freedom to sin. We discussed that a little bit last week.
 
But we do have freedom in Christ. We do have the, it's like we don't have to apply the law daily to our lives, the Ten Commandments, in order to be saved. But the law is written on our hearts so that we have the freedom to know what is right and what's wrong, and then do the right and shun the wrong.
 
But we have to understand that even though he's not talking about things immoral, things wrong per se, we have liberty, but we have to understand liberty is not a license. You can't say, you know, I've trusted Christ as my Savior. By grace, I've been saved through faith.
 
Now if I go out and sin, don't matter, I'm going to heaven anyway. No. If you read any bit of Scripture at all, you'll find out that's not true.
 
Although I've known Christians that feel that way. Oh, I sinned a little bit, ain't no big deal. It is a big deal because you violated God's desires.
 
So as we deal with people, either believers, whether they're weak believers, strong believers, whether they're unbelievers, he's going to give us some ideas of how to do so. Here in verse 23, he says, all things are lawful, all things are not expedient, all things are lawful, and all things edify not. Here's two rules to help us to decide.
 
Any situation, especially when you're dealing with other people, but it could also be in your own life. You feel like doing something and you're asking yourself a question. Man, should I be doing this? First question, is it expedient? In other words, does it work together for the good of everybody? Is it a worthwhile endeavor? Is it something that will not embarrass either you or the Lord? Is it expedient? Many things, although they may seem harmless, could be hurtful to someone who is either weak in the faith or close to the faith.
 
I remember a story years ago, I hope I get it right, about a pastor's meeting in some big hotel, a whole group of pastors that got together for a week of learning and fellowshipping and exhorting one another. And one of the pastors had been talking to the desk clerk, and every day he witnessed to him. And he was getting closer and closer for the desk clerk to understand and maybe accept the Lord.
 
The last day, this pastor went to the desk clerk as he's checking out and says, have you decided to trust the Lord? And the desk clerk said, no, I'm not going to do that. And he goes, why? He says, well, you'd almost convinced me that trusting Christ was important, that being a Christian and living a Christian life was important. Then as I'm checking out pastors, I found so many of you pastors who'd signed up for pornography pay-per-view on the TV that I said to myself, what's the use? They live the same way I do.
 
And so we have to be careful. How many times have we said something, done something that we thought, well, that's real holy, and yet it didn't draw someone closer to Christ and drew them further away. Remember, God does call us to be holy, but not holier than now.
 
And there's a difference. And so here he says all things, first of all, is it expedient? What am I, if what I'm doing, if one of the believers I know or someone I've been trying to witness to, will it drive them further from Christ or closer to him? Second one is, does it edify? That means building somebody up, either in faith or building them up in love, building them up in their worship for God. In Romans chapter 15, verse 1 and 2, it says, we then that are strong ought to bear the infirmities of the weak and not to please ourselves.
 
Let every one of us please his neighbor for his good to edification. Everything we do should be done to try to build people up, especially on other believers. Ephesians 4:29, let no, even in what we say, let no corrupt communication proceed out of your mouth, but that which is the good to the use of edifying, that it may minister grace unto the hearers.
 
When you're talking to a group, the things you say and the way you say them, do you draw them closer to Christ or not? I see this especially in my life, others' lives, and the way we, if you still have kids in the house, how do you treat your kids? Are you always yelling and screaming at them? Does that build them up? I'm not saying you shouldn't correct them, but there's a difference in how we do so. You know, I heard a story once of another illustration about a guy had been trying to invite his neighbor to church, and the neighbor kept saying no, and finally guy says, why won't you go to church with me? He says, I see what you say to your kids before trying to get them in the car. And he says, I don't need to go there to be able to act like that, I act like that already.
 
So let no corrupt communication, nothing that will be for less than building up somebody else. How about listening to others? First Timothy 1:4, neither give heed to fables and endless genealogies which minister questions rather than godly edifying which is in the faith.
 
Have you, you know, I mentioned this a lot, I'm addicted to Facebook, especially groups, Christian groups and pastor's groups where we have discussions. And sometimes when I read what some people believe, I want to get involved and go, what are you thinking? Sometimes I just, I honestly, I go, show me the verse that backs that up. But sometimes we listen to all these fables, listen to all these false teachings, and we realize that does nothing to build other people up.
 
So two rules to help us decide how to deal with other people. Does it edify? Is it expedient? Now he goes on to tell us in verse 24, that no man seek his own but every man's another's wealth. Our affections, or I'm sorry, our actions can affect other people.
 
Philippians 2:4 and 5. It says, look not every man on his own things, but every man also on the things of others. Let this mind be in you, which is also in Christ Jesus. And Philippians 2:21, for all seek their own, not the things which are Christ Jesus.
 
When we're dealing with other people, we have to think about them. We have to think, am I acting like Christ when I deal with these people? Say, well, they're just a bunch of sinners. They don't really care.
 
God cares. And God knows that maybe you're the one that's going to lead them to Jesus Christ. But if you act like a sinner yourself and say, I'm saved, they're going to just thumb their nose and go, I don't see the big deal. Why should I do that? So we have to look every man on his own things, but on others, so we can help build them up, help encourage them. Then he goes on to discuss a little bit about what to do if you're invited to dinner. You have an unbeliever, or maybe a very weak believer, that invites you to dinner, and they may be serving some things, some meat that they bought that was offered to idols.
 
Well, Paul's recommendations are very clear. First of all, in verse 27, if any of them that believe not bid you to a feast and you'd be disposed to go, I almost look at disposed to go as meaning you have no other choice. You ever had dinners like that? It's like, man, I can't say no.
 
Whatsoever said before you eat, asking no question for conscience sake, but if any man saying to you, this is offered to sacrifice to idols, eat not for his sake that showed it, and for conscience sake, for the earth is the Lord and the fullness thereof. Conscience I say not thy own, but of the others, for why is my liberty judged of another man's conscience? For if I be by grace be a partaker, why am I evil spoken of for that which I give thanks? Paul's here saying, listen, somebody invites you over to dinner, and you know the meat they're serving was offered to idols. Don't bring it up.
 
Just eat it, is what he's saying. Just eat the meat. Because if you bring it up, and you start the discussion, what's going to happen? Now you're going to get that person start thinking about sacrificing to idols and pull them further from God.
 
He says just, and I know for some of you it's kind of hard, just keep your mouth shut. Don't ask any questions. However, if they volunteer, how's that meat? It was offered to idols.
 
He says, don't eat it. He says, if they don't tell you, it's okay to eat. Earth, everything belongs to the Lord, right? But if they do tell you, don't eat it.
 
Why? Well, it's because we're looking out for the conscience of somebody else. Because we don't want people worshiping idols. We're trying to lead them to the Lord, right? And so we see this in our world today.
 
Maybe not worship to idols per se, but things that people worship that they may try to get you to do also. And you want to turn to Romans chapter one. Well, see, this is what's happening a lot.
 
In Romans chapter one, starting with verse 23, it says, they changed the glory of the incorruptible God into an image made like the corruptible man and the birds and four-footed beast and creeping things. Wherefore, God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lust of their own hearts to dishonor their own bodies between themselves, who changed the truth of God into a lie. And listen, and worshiped and served the creature more than the creator who was blessed forever and ever. Amen.
 
So many times people worship the creator or creation, the creature and they forget that God's the one who created them all. This could affect us in many different ways.
 
And it could cause us, if we're not careful, to discuss things with people that may anger them, may not. I don't know what your views are personally. Let's say climate control, climate change, all right? It's changing.
 
What's a Christian's perspective? God says the earth is yours. Take care of it. But on the other hand, sometimes they get a little crazy.
 
And some of the rules we have, you can check this yourself, I was reading the other day. In China, they've just built 149 coal-fired plants to make parts of batteries and solar panels to sell to the United States so we feel good about ourselves.
 
Check the Weather Channel. This is my favorite. They can't tell what the weather's going to be today or tomorrow. How can they tell me in 10 years what it's going to be? Does that mean we don't take care of our environment? We don't take care of our world? Yes, we do.
 
We try to do the best we can. But let's not be crazy about it. I know some people don't eat meat.
 
That's fine. But if they don't for their own religious purposes and they come to your house and say, you know, we're only having salad, don't say, where's the meat, if you know they don't eat it. Just eat the salad.
 
Because our purpose is to look out for their conscience, their moral compass, not your own. You know or you should know what's right and wrong. The Word of God tells us.
 
You should know you have freedom to do things like eat meat offered to idols. So you don't do it for your own conscience, you know better. But if they don't know better, you may be pushing them further and further from God because you make a big deal out of it.
 
Sometimes we do things in the name of religion that just totally frustrates me. You know, I hate the fact that there were a Baptist church. Remember that Baptist church that was waiting for planes to fly in with dead soldiers and sailors on it? And then they would hold protests there and say it was because America was so bad that's why these people died.
 
How does that edify and build people up? I know a church is that if they find out someone's homosexual, they just assume you can just die. We don't care. No, they're a soul that God wants to see saved too.
 
Do we agree with their lifestyle? No, it's not according to Scripture. But they're still a person who Christ died for and they need him. So many of the things we do, just stop and ask yourself, if I do this or don't do this, how am I affecting what they think about God? I know that's a lot sometimes, but that's what he's saying.
 
What I'm doing, how will it affect what that person thinks about God, their conscience? But then he goes on and kind of summarizes everything in verse 31. Whether therefore you eat or drink or whatsoever you do, do all to the glory of God. How can we do the glory of God? That means the way you honor God, the way you praise God, the way you worship God, everything should be done with God at the forefront.
 
What does God think about what I'm doing? Does he get honor from this? Does he get glory from this? And it says, whatever you eat or whatever you drink, whatever you do, it's for God's glory. You know, I mentioned before my favorite verse I've had for a long time. I heard Will here quote it a couple of weeks ago, Colossians 3:23, whatever you do, do it heartily as to the Lord and not unto men.
 
So everything we do, we want to give God the glory. So everything we do, we say, I'm not doing it for my boss. I'm doing it for God.
 
I'm not doing it for my family. I'm doing it for God. Will they get good from it? Absolutely.
 
But God gets the glory. Everything we do should give God the glory for our good. And it's pretty plain.
 
Whatever you do, eating, drinking, do it for the glory of God, being able to praise him. I'll be honest with you. When you get done doing something, it's a whole lot more fun to praise God for allowing you to participate than doing something he don't want and have to ask his forgiveness because you sinned.
 
One of them, you can look him directly in the face and the other is like a little kid, you come looking down at the floor, ashamed of what you did. Do all for the glory of God. In fact, he continues, give none offense, neither Jew or Gentile or Church of God.
 
None offense doesn't mean, that just means don't on purpose try to offend people. It gets harder and harder when you try to share the word of God not to offend people, but try not to offend them. Learn to say things from scripture in a way like the Bible tells in Ephesians, speaking the truth in love. And that's how we do it. God has given believers the responsibility to share Christ with the world. And so we are to act like Christ in the world.
 
Will you offend people sometimes? Yes, it's inevitable. But do you do it on purpose? I hope not. Why? You know, it's like we talked about the dinner.
 
You don't get invited to dinner going, you're serving some of that meat offered to idols. Well, if you do, I'm not coming. No, that's offensive.
 
Because if you invite them to meal, you're saying, why? Remember when Jesus was invited to meals with sinners? Why did he go? So he could tell them about himself. And maybe we'll get the opportunity if we're invited to meals with sinners, not to participate in their sins, but not to agree with their sins, but to be able to share the good news of Jesus Christ. And that's what he tells us here in verse 33.
 
Even as I please all men and all things, not seeking my own profit, but the profit of many, that they may be saved. Everything we do, we do for the glory of God so that people will trust Jesus Christ. That's our purpose on earth.
 
I don't know if you knew that, because personally, the day I got saved, I wish he'd have taken me to heaven. It has saved a whole lot of heartbreak, but he didn't. He said, all right, now you are my representative on earth.
 
You are an ambassador for Christ. You are left here to see people trust me as savior also. But if you go about trying to get your own profit, your own way all the time instead of mine, it's not going to happen.
 
If you go around trying to prove that you're holier than everybody else, it's not going to happen. Instead, we have to look out for other people, consider their feelings, consider what they think, not to agree with their sin, never to agree with their sin. However, realizing that they are a sinner just like you were.
 
Their sin may be different than yours is, but if they die in their sins, they're still going to hell. You know, the homosexual, you say, well, there are some churches go where they deserve to go to hell. They don't deserve to go to hell any more than the old lady.
 
All she ever did in her life was lie. They need Jesus Christ. And so Paul is saying, listen, you want to lead people to Christ? Do all for the glory of God.
 
When you deal with people, try your best to do things that are expedient for their good, to do things that will edify, build them up and think about the other person. As I was working on this message, I thought to myself, over the years, if all of the people who had called themselves Christians had been concerned with how other people see Christ instead of just trying to make their way number one, think how much different the world is today. You're not your own.
 
You belong to Christ. So let's live that way. Amen.
 
And let's start thinking about, before you say something, before you do something, what is the effect on the person I'm dealing with? Just be like Christ. Let's bow our heads. I don't know how the Lord spoke to your heart today.
 
The most important thing is, do you know Jesus Christ as your personal Lord and Savior? If you were to die today, would you be in heaven? You're that sure you're salvation. If you're not, you need to get things right with the Lord. Jesus Christ came and died on that cross, shed his blood and was buried.
 
He rose the third day and he did it all so that when you trusted what he did for you by faith, your sins are forgiven. Then once they're forgiven, you're expected to live a certain way. Now you start thinking about how other people see Christ.
 
Now you start acting in a way that other people see Christ through you. And the way you talk, the way you act, the way you respond, are you doing it the right way? Are you doing it the way Christ wants us to? Let's go to Lord in prayer. As I'm praying, you can pray.
 
You know what's on your heart. You know what you need to talk to the Lord about. Let's pray together.
 
Heavenly Father, Lord, we thank you for your word and what it teaches us. We thank you, Lord, that we are told to love one another. And in this section, we're taught how we can do that.
 
We can do that by caring enough for the other person, especially for unbelievers, that the things we do will not drive them from you, Lord, but draw them to you. Help us, Lord, to be the kind of people you want us to be. Help us, Lord, to be children, your children, that go out and reach the world one person at a time.
 
We're thankful again, Lord, for working in our hearts. We're thankful, Lord, for the salvation we have. We're thankful, Lord, that you forgive sins.
 
And we're thankful, Lord, we're able to gather together to praise you. In Jesus' name, amen.

Sermon Outline:

I. Love must be sincere and good (v. 9)
II. Believers should treat one another as family (v. 10)
III. We must be diligent in serving the Lord (v. 11)
IV. We should rejoice in hope and pray in trouble (v. 12)
V. We should meet needs and show hospitality (v. 13)

Romans chapter 12, continuing on our study in Romans. We started noticing last week, and I thought it was interesting, Marilyn mentioned in her presentation, the importance of really discipling and discipleship and following the Lord. And that's what we started last week. 

Here in Romans 12, I believe it is talking about how to be a good disciple. You know, many people, they'll get saved, they'll trust the Lord, and then they'll just do what they want for the rest of their lives, thinking that they're okay. They got a ticket to heaven, they can do what they want. 

But no, God expects us to be disciples. He expects us to follow his teaching and to emulate it with those that we run into, to duplicate it. So last week, as we were looking at really Romans verse 3 through 18 in different parts, we saw 3 and 8 last week, where we learned about the unity of the body, we learned about the gifts of the Spirit.

Today, we have part number 2, and it centers on the believer's outward actions toward others. As a disciple, let's read verses 9 through 13, and we'll go back and look at them probably pretty quickly. Verse 9, let love be without dissimilation.

Abhor that which is evil, cling to that which is good, cleave to that which is good. Be kindly affectioned one to another with brotherly love, and honor preferring one another, not slothful in business, fervent in spirit, serving the Lord. Rejoicing in hope, patient in tribulation, continuing instant in prayer, distributing to the necessity of saints, given to hospitality. 

These are all things that show that we are a follower of Christ because we are showing others really Christlikeness, being like Jesus. Let's look at each of these a little bit individually. It starts out in verse 9, let love be without dissimilation. 

It's a big word. It just really means love that is sincere, love that is unfeigned, love that is without hypocrisy. Literally, it means love that is so real that it's spontaneous in your life. 

You don't have, you meet a brother or sister in Christ, and most of these are talking about our relationship with other brothers and sisters, but those that aren't believers are going to see that. But when you meet another brother and sister, you don't have to decide am I going to show love toward them or not. If you have love that's without dissimilation, if you have love of Christ, it will be automatic. 

Now when we talk about love here, sometimes people get a little confused because there's a bunch of different kind of loves. There's a love between a man and a woman in marriage, but that's not what this is talking about. This is the same kind of love as for God so loved the world. 

This is a love that really sometimes is translated, especially like in 1 Corinthians, translated when we read the word charity, and that to me that's the best way to understand what this word love means because we know what charity means. Charity is when you see someone who has a need and you help them with that need regardless of who they are and regardless of whether they can pay you back or not. You help them because they need help. 

That's charity and that's the kind of love here. You love somebody else because they are a brother and sister in Christ. You're saying, well what if they're sinning? What if they're doing this? What if they're doing that? We'll cover that in a minute, but Jesus in John 13 35, he said, by this shall all men know that you are my disciples if you have love one toward another.

And we're not talking again about the mushy love. We're talking about love that is an action word, looking out for other people to see if you can help or just to be with them. But sometimes you're saying, well what about the actions? What about the way they're living? What if they're living in sin? Do I still have to love them? It depends. 

Do they still have needs that you can meet sometimes? Are they willing to be with you? You see, we're supposed to, you've heard the old saying and a lot of people like to discount it, love the person but not what they're doing all the time. That's why the next part of this verse talks about that. Abhor that which is evil. 

Cleave to that which is good. You know, there's a lot of evil in our world, amen? And so our love is to be unfeigned. It's to be real, but it's not a love that covers and overlooks the sin in somebody's life. 

We're to abhor that which is evil. That's quite the word, abhor. You know what I mean? That means to detest utterly. 

You know, I don't know about you, but I abhor snakes. I see a snake is like, I like to be around them. My brother, on the other hand, he'd hold them and put them in his pocket.

Abhor evil. Don't think that you have to put up with the evil in somebody's life to still love them. You abhor it and you stand up for God's word. 

It really bugs me when somebody says, I'm a homosexual, but I'm a Christian. You can't be unless you're trying to stop the homosexual acts, okay? Or my favorite, I was born this way. You know what I tell people? You're right. 

The Bible says for all have sinned and come short of the glory of God. It's just that some people's sins are different than others. Homosexuality is a sin.

So is drunkenness. So is fornication. So is so many other things. 

We're all born sinners, but thank God we don't have to stay that way. That's why we're born again, so we don't do that anymore. But we're to abhor that which is evil. 

Stand up against it. Detest it. Tell people, no, God says that's an abomination. 

But on the other hand, you can't just spend your whole life hating evil because people will think you're weird. You also have to cleave that at which is good. You know, we've been studying the seven churches in Revelation, and we've made the note that when Jesus speaks to each of the churches, or most of them, he always tells them what they're doing good before he tells them what they're doing wrong. 

Look for good in people. Cleave to it. That's what God wants us to do. 

To cleave to that which is good. To cleave to that which is honest. To cleave to that which is good to help people out. 

That word good really means to be beneficial. What can help people to grow, help people to survive. Cleave to it. 

So when you have a love that's like Christ, you have to have a love that chooses between good and evil. Choose the good. Abhor the evil. 

But the love also is in verse 10, be kindly affection one to another with brotherly love and honor preferring one another. So we should have a love that is kindly affection with brotherly love. That word kindly affection means treat somebody like family.

You know, I've been in churches, perhaps you've been in churches, where you have one group of people sit over here, and one group of people sit here, and one group sit over there, and they're like little cliques, and they don't want to talk to each other. These people say they're saved, but they're better than this group. And this people say they're saved, but they're better in both groups. 

And that people say they're saved, and they don't even want to talk to anybody. But if we're brothers and sisters in Christ, and scripture says we are, amen, we should be willing to treat each other like brothers and sisters. You say, but wait a minute, I got a brother, I got a sister, we fight occasionally.

Yeah, but if you're really good brothers and sisters, you'll make up too. You realize one of you was wrong. I know my brother and my sister sometimes have arguments.

Soon they realize that I'm the one that's always right, and they're the ones that, no, I'm just, but you know what I mean. We treat each other like we're brothers and sisters. And it goes to a point where in honor preferring one another. 

If you're a believer, if you're a disciple of Jesus Christ, you should want to be around other brothers and sisters in Christ instead of around people that just live in the world. Because you're saying, I know, but Jesus, he hung out with sinners and publicans, but he didn't let them affect his life. He was there to tell them they need him. 

And so if you're going to hang out with some people to witness to them, to share the gospel of Jesus Christ, to try to show them the errors of their ways, that's one thing. But if you're just hanging out with them because, well, they're people I grew up with. They're my friends from school. 

They're just, you know, I know they're doing bad things, but if you prefer them more than God's family, you need to check yourself and ask yourself why. Because we are to prefer one another. You should, you know, I like what Marilyn said in her missions, the kids want to be in church.

They want to come to prayer meeting. They want to be around other believers. And that's the way we all should be. 

We should be looking forward to coming here on Sunday morning and Sunday afternoon and Wednesday, not just to hear the word of God being preached and being taught, but so we can be around other believers because, you know, you may have a problem. That's fine. You share it with other people and you never know who may be able to help you overcome that problem. 

You may never know who may be able to say, you know, I had something similar to this and this is how God worked in my life. Because that's what we do. We should honor or in honor prefer one another. 

Amen. But not just being a disciple requires love, requires showing that love by hanging out with other people who are brothers and sisters in Christ. But living the life of disciple also requires or involves being an example to those around us. 

And that's why I believe what these other verses are trying to say. How can you be a good example? Told some of you this story before. My first submarine, I told people I was a Christian. 

I hadn't been living as a Christian for a while and suddenly I rededicated my life to the Lord and started living like a Christian. I had one guy who watched me like a hawk. Everything I did or everything I said, if it wasn't his idea what a Christian should be, he'd go, is that the way a Christian should act? Is that the way a Christian should talk? It got to be really aggravating.

But on the other hand, because people watch you, I prayed before every meal. You're saying, but there was nobody around. There were other Christians to watch you. 

God was. I prayed before every meal and I'd been witnessing to one of my bosses. And about a year later, we were having a party over at his house and his wife was saved. 

She was charismatic, but I talked to her. I think she was, she was just a little confused. And as soon as I got to the door, you know what the first thing she said? John got saved. 

Really? And she said, and it's all because of you. I go, what do you mean? I tried witnessing. He wouldn't listen to me. 

She go, no, he watched you. He watched you say you were a Christian. He watched you practice it by praying for every meal. 

And he suddenly realized that's what I need. People are watching you and you're going to be an example, whether a good example or a bad example of what a Christian should be. If you're a bad example, what a Christian should be, the chance of winning them to Christ is a lot slimmer than if you are a good example of what a Christian should be. 

Amen. I know that's hard to take sometimes, but that's the truth. Notice, and we got to hurry up. 

Marilyn, you spoke way too, no, I just, everybody's getting hungry, but that's okay. Notice, first of all, verse 11, here's how we can be example, not slothful in business. Now that word business in the King James doesn't mean the same as it does now. 

It doesn't mean business as in at work, although that is some, that is a truth. You know, you shouldn't be lazy at work and then say you're a Christian because the boss will just sort of, yeah, right. No, this means really business means your purpose or your spiritual business. 

Don't be lazy in your Christianity. Don't be lazy in your spiritual life. But even if you took it the other way, you know, everything in our life as a believer, it's either spiritual or it's either secular or sacred. 

But the truth is a spiritual person will make even the secular sacred, but a secular person will make even the sacred unspiritual. You need to serve the Lord. You need to be not lazy in being a believer. 

And it goes on to say, fervent in spirit, that means on fire for the Lord. You're saying, you mean I got to go down a street corner and preach like all these street preachers do? No, but you should have that little flame of the Holy Spirit burning within you, willing to give anyone an answer when they ask, willing to see when somebody has a need so you can share that love, willing to look at others. And this is something that's always been hard for me. 

When you see somebody else for the first time, whether they're sinning or not, it's your first thought, they need Jesus Christ. You look at their soul. They need Christ. 

People you meet on the job, they need Christ. And the only example they may have is you. Are you fervent in spirit? Are you on fire for the Lord? It says serving the Lord. 

Like Marilyn said, even the kids, they like to serve the Lord and what you're teaching. Even if it's washing chairs or getting ready for a picnic, which some of them are out there doing now. Or whatever you do, everything, you should be on fire for the Lord and everything you do is serving the Lord. 

Remember I said for our afternoon service, what we're going to do is share our favorite verses. Serving the Lord. My favorite verse is Colossians 3.23. Whatever you do, he knows it. 

Whatever you do, do it heartily, as to the Lord and not in the men. No matter what you do, whether it's working, whether it's driving a truck, whether it's going to school, whether being a missionary, everything you do is not for you and it's not for the one you're working for. It's for him. 

You get that in your mind, it'll change everything. You're serving the Lord. It goes on. 

How else can we be an example? Rejoicing in hope. You look at the things that we see in the newspaper and on the news, you're going, man, there's no hope for this country. You're right. 

There's no hope for anybody on earth unless they know Jesus Christ. And sometimes when, you know, because it goes with patience and tribulation, continuing instant prayer, those three go together. When problems happen in your life, troubles, tribulation, persecution, rejoice in hope.

This world is not my home. I'm only passing through. You're not a citizen of the earth.

You're a citizen of heaven. One day, all of this will go away and you'll be with him. You have the hope of eternal life. 

You're saying, yeah, but these problems are so pressing. We've been going through the Old Testament. We find out that any time there's battles to come up, first thing they did when they did the right thing was ask God, should I fight this battle or shouldn't I? And if God said, fight that battle, he said, I'm going to go before you and win it for you. 

But if he said not to, and they did anyway, they get whooped. That's why it's weird to be instant in prayer, patient in tribulations, but instant in prayer. No matter what happens in your life, always go to the Lord and say, Lord, guide me in handling this problem. 

You know what? He will. You say, well, how do you know? Because I've seen it happen in my life. I've seen it happen in other people's lives.

Now, be prepared. The answer you want may not always be the answer God gives you, but be prepared to follow his guidance. Instant in prayer. 

First Thessalonians, it says, pray without ceasing. Always be in communication with God. You're having problems, you're having tribulation, you're having persecution, just having troubles in your life, just pray. 

Or as I like to tell people sometimes, just look up, keep looking up, because that's where your hope is, in heaven. Keep looking up. And I guarantee you, when you're having problems and you tell people you're a Christian, they're going to be watching how you handle those problems. 

Handle them in a godly way, handle them in a spiritual way, handle them with the guidance of the Holy Spirit. And finally, it says, distributing to the necessity of saints, giving to hospitality. That just means if someone, a brother or sister in Christ has a definite need, and you can supply that need, help out. 

Giving to hospitality means, giving to, the word hospitality actually means to entertain, you know, hospitality in the old days, and when the Bible was written, there weren't hotels a lot, there were a few inns, but even Jesus couldn't get in that one, or Mary and Joseph couldn't, so people would keep them in a home, but today there's hotels. But more what that means, giving to hospitality, just means be willing to fellowship with other believers, especially those who just sometimes need to talk, need to spend time with somebody to air their problems. Yeah, we pray, but it's all so awful helpful to get wisdom and guidance from other believers, and you should be willing to help. 

Somebody calls you, somebody contacts you and says, hey, can we talk? Nope, sorry, too busy. That happens. Try to make a time, because God didn't lead them to you just so you could turn them away, so we can be an example that way, especially with people we work with or family members, because they're going to be looking at you. 

First of all, they're going to be looking at you and see how you, you know, if you're supposed to be following a God who is love, following that, they're going to be looking at you and saying they're not very loving, but they're going to be looking at you and say, boy, they're starting to practice the love of God, but a whore that which is evil, cleave to that which is good. Be an example to those around you and try to realize that God wants his family to be together, to learn from one another, to encourage one another, to lift up one another. God wants you to be an example to those around you.

By the way you handle problems, by the way you live your Christian life. So the question is right now, how good a disciple are you? Are you kind of the disciple that would match these things we just looked at, or are you the kind of disciple that says, I've kind of fallen short on a few of these, I need to really go to the Lord and ask for help in doing these? Because honestly, what the world needs is people who not just say they're Christians, they need people who live like a Christian. Amen? We're happy we have missionaries like John and Marilyn going to other places to teach them to accept the Lord, to teach them how to be disciples so that they can show that love to other people. 

Our mission field is here. Be a disciple. Let's bow our heads please. 

Just ask yourself, do you love in such a way that it's spontaneous, it's instantaneous, we're other brothers and sisters in Christ? Do you prefer to be around other brothers and sisters in Christ? Do you prefer that? Do you live a life where you're on fire for the Lord, you want to serve the Lord in no matter what capacity? Are you living a life where you look forward to either the Lord coming back or Him calling you home? You have that hope of eternal life? Are you praying all the time? The only one that can answer that is you. So as we go to Lord in prayer right now, talk to the Lord. Praise Him for the things you've been able to do. 

Seek encouragement and guidance for the things you still need to do. The world needs Jesus. Like somebody said once, the only Jesus many of them will see is you, Heavenly Father.

Lord, we thank you for your word and Lord there's a lot here for us to think about, to learn, to put into our life so we can be a disciple of Jesus Christ. We're thankful Lord that you show us these things so we know how to live a life that's Christ-like, to live a life that gives you glory and you honor, to live a life to show others that Jesus and salvation is real. Help us Lord to be better.

Help us Lord to be more like you. In Jesus' name we pray. Amen.
